questions.q: Unless a different relationship is established in writing, a Florida real estate licensee is presumed to be operating as a:
questions.ex: Florida presumes a transaction-broker relationship unless a single agent or no brokerage relationship is established in writing.

0: Single agency must be established in writing.
1: Dual agency is illegal in Florida.
3: Subagency is not one of Florida's authorized relationships.

questions.q: A brokerage is a single agent for a seller. The same brokerage's buyer customer wants to buy the property. How may the brokerage lawfully proceed?
c: Continue as single agent for the seller and also become single agent for the buyer
Act as a dual agent for both parties after both sign a written dual-agency consent
Obtain the seller's written consent to transition, then act as transaction broker for both
Refer the buyer to another brokerage, because Florida forbids working both sides
questions.ex: A brokerage may not be a single agent for both sides. With the principal's prior written consent to transition, it may act as a transaction broker for both.

0: Single agency for both sides is dual agency, which Florida prohibits.
1: Consent does not legalize dual agency in Florida.
3: Florida provides a lawful path (transition to transaction broker).

questions.q: In a transaction-broker relationship, the buyer is a:
questions.ex: A transaction broker provides limited representation and is not a fiduciary; the party is a customer. Only a single agent has a principal.

0: Principal is the term for a single agent's client.
2: The licensee, not the buyer, would be the fiduciary in single agency.
3: Subagency is not an authorized Florida relationship.

questions.q: Which duty is owed by a single agent but NOT by a transaction broker?
c: Presenting all offers and counteroffers in a timely manner
questions.ex: Loyalty, obedience, full confidentiality and full disclosure belong only to the single agent. The other three choices are owed by transaction brokers too.

0: Honesty is owed in every relationship.
1: Accounting is owed in every relationship.
3: Presenting offers is a transaction-broker duty too.

questions.q: How many duties does a licensee owe a party with whom there is NO brokerage relationship?
questions.ex: No brokerage relationship: 3 duties (honesty, disclosure of known material facts on residential property, accounting). Transaction broker 7; single agent 9.

questions.q: A seller tells her transaction broker she would accept $20,000 less than list price. The broker tells a buyer, hoping to close quickly. Which duty did the broker breach?
c: No duty, because transaction brokers are neutral
questions.ex: Limited confidentiality forbids revealing that the seller will accept less than the asking price (unless waived in writing).

0: Loyalty is owed only by a single agent.
2: Obedience is owed only by a single agent.

questions.q: Which is part of a transaction broker's duty of limited confidentiality?
c: Not disclosing that a buyer is willing to pay more than the offered price
Not disclosing known latent defects the seller asked to keep confidential
Not presenting low offers the seller has said she would find insulting
Not accounting to either party for deposits until the day of closing
questions.ex: Limited confidentiality protects price flexibility, motivation and information a party asks to keep confidential. It never permits hiding material defects or withholding offers or funds.

1: Known material defects on residential property must be disclosed in every relationship.
2: All offers must be presented in a timely manner.
3: Funds must be accounted for at all times.

questions.q: A seller instructs his single agent: 'Don't mention the foundation crack you saw.' What must the agent do?
c: Obey the instruction, because obedience is one of the single agent's duties
Disclose the known material defect; obedience covers lawful instructions only
Stay silent about the crack unless the buyer asks a direct question about it
Withdraw from the listing and keep the information confidential permanently
questions.ex: Obedience is limited to lawful instructions. Disclosure of known facts materially affecting the value of residential property is owed in all relationships.

0: Obedience never covers an unlawful instruction.
2: The duty does not depend on the buyer asking.
3: Confidentiality does not cover concealing known material defects.

questions.q: When must a Single Agent Notice be given?
c: At or before closing, together with the other closing documents the parties sign
Before or when a listing/representation agreement is signed, or before a showing, whichever is first
Within 24 hours after the first showing, or after a representation agreement is signed, if later
Only when the customer asks in writing which brokerage relationship applies
questions.ex: The single agent notice must be given before or at the time of entering into a listing or representation agreement, or before showing property, whichever occurs first.

3: It is mandatory in residential sales.

questions.q: Which brokerage relationship requires NO written disclosure in Florida?
questions.ex: Transaction broker is the presumed relationship and requires no disclosure.

1: A No Brokerage Relationship Notice is required before showing.
3: Designated sales associates require signed disclosures.

questions.q: In which transaction are Florida's brokerage relationship disclosure requirements applicable?
questions.ex: Disclosures apply to residential sales: ≤4 units, unimproved land for ≤4 units, or agricultural property ≤10 acres. Leases (without an option to buy), 5+ units and auctions are outside.

0: Rentals and leases are excluded unless they include an option to purchase ≤4 units.

questions.q: The brokerage relationship disclosure requirements apply to residential sales. In which situation do they NOT apply at all?
c: Showing a buyer a single-family home after she called the office about the listing
Answering general questions at a bona fide open house, with no confidential or price talk
Taking an exclusive-right-of-sale listing on a duplex owned by two investors
Showing a buyer an unimproved lot that is zoned for one single-family home
questions.ex: Bona fide open houses with no confidential information, offer, or representation agreement are exempt. The other choices are residential sales activities, where the rules apply (a notice is then needed if the licensee acts as a single agent or with no brokerage relationship; the transaction-broker default needs none).

0: Showing residential property requires a disclosure (before showing).
3: Unimproved land intended for ≤4 units is residential.

questions.q: The Consent to Transition to Transaction Broker must be signed by the principal:
c: at closing, along with all of the other transaction documents
before the licensee changes from single agent to transaction broker
only if the customer on the other side requests it in writing
within 10 days after the licensee begins acting as transaction broker
questions.ex: The principal must consent in writing before the change from single agent to transaction broker.

2: It is the principal's consent, and it is required.
3: Consent must come before the change.

questions.q: Which fact does Florida law declare NOT material, so a licensee need not disclose it?
c: The roof leaks during heavy rain
A homicide occurred in the house
questions.ex: Florida law (s. 689.25) provides that a homicide, suicide or death on the property, and an occupant's HIV/AIDS status, are not material facts. Physical defects that affect value must be disclosed.

0: A hidden roof leak is a latent material defect.
2: A failing seawall materially affects value.

questions.q: A broker may appoint designated sales associates for the buyer and the seller when:
c: the transaction is residential and both parties agree in writing to the arrangement
the deal is nonresidential and buyer and seller each have assets of $1 million or more
the sale price of the property, residential or commercial, exceeds $1 million
the broker or one of the sales associates owns an interest in the property
questions.ex: Designated sales associates are available only in nonresidential transactions where both buyer and seller have assets of $1 million or more (and request it in writing).

2: The test is each party's assets, not the price.
3: Ownership by the broker is unrelated.

questions.q: After a listing expires, a buyer asks the former listing broker what price the seller had said she would accept. The broker had been a single agent. Which is correct?
c: The broker may answer, because all duties ended when the listing expired
The broker must not answer; confidentiality survives the end of the relationship
The broker may answer if the buyer signs a buyer-brokerage agreement first
The broker must answer, because the duty of honesty requires full answers
questions.ex: Confidentiality (and the duty to account) survives the end of the brokerage relationship.

3: Honesty does not require revealing a former principal's confidential information.

questions.q: A seller in an 'AS IS' sale knows his Florida home's slab is cracked and the crack is hidden under carpet. Must he disclose it?
c: No, because an AS IS contract means the buyer accepts every defect
No, unless the buyer's home inspector discovers the crack during inspection
Yes, known hidden defects that materially affect value must be disclosed, AS IS or not
Only if the buyer uses FHA financing, which requires a full disclosure form
questions.ex: Under Johnson v. Davis the seller must disclose known latent defects that materially affect value. An AS IS contract shifts repair obligations, not the disclosure duty.

0: AS IS does not cancel the duty to disclose known hidden defects.
1: The duty exists regardless of the inspection.

questions.q: A sales associate receives an earnest money check on Thursday. There are no holidays. By when must the broker deposit it?
questions.ex: The associate delivers it to the broker by end of the next business day (Friday). The broker deposits by the end of the third business day after the brokerage received it — the day of receipt does not count: Friday (1), Monday (2), Tuesday (3).

0: End of Friday is the associate's deadline to deliver to the broker.
3: Counting the weekend or the day of receipt gives the wrong day; Tuesday is business day 3.

questions.q: How much of the broker's own money may be kept in a sales escrow account to cover bank charges?
questions.ex: Up to $1,000 in a sales escrow account; up to $5,000 in a property management escrow account. More is commingling.

3: A limited amount is allowed for bank charges.

questions.q: A broker uses $3,000 from the escrow account to pay the office rent, planning to put it back next week. This is:
c: a minor violation subject only to a notice of noncompliance
questions.ex: Using escrow funds for personal or business purposes is conversion — more serious than commingling (merely mixing funds).

0: Commingling is mixing funds; spending them is conversion.
2: There is no repayment grace period.
3: Misuse of trust funds is serious misconduct.

questions.q: A broker may place escrow funds in an interest-bearing account only if:
c: the broker discloses that the brokerage will keep all of the interest
all parties consent in writing (including who receives the interest)
the deposit exceeds $10,000 and will be held for more than 30 days
the FREC approves the bank and the account in advance, in writing
questions.ex: Interest-bearing escrow accounts require written consent of all parties, which also states who gets the interest.

0: The broker may not unilaterally keep the interest.
3: FREC approval is not the requirement.

questions.q: After receiving conflicting demands for an escrow deposit, a broker must notify the FREC in writing within:
questions.ex: Notice within 15 business days of the last demand; a settlement procedure must be instituted within 30 business days.

0: 10 business days is the notice if the dispute settles before an EDO issues.
2: 30 business days is the deadline to institute a settlement procedure.

questions.q: A title company holds the deposit in a failed sale and both buyer and seller demand it. Which statement is correct?
c: The broker must notify the FREC and request an escrow disbursement order
No escrow disbursement order is available, because the broker does not hold the funds
The broker must have the title company move the deposit into the brokerage's account
The broker must instruct the title company to release the deposit to the seller
questions.ex: An escrow disbursement order is available only when the broker holds the funds. When a title company or attorney holds the deposit, the FREC notice-and-procedure rule does not apply to the broker.

0: An EDO requires the funds to be in the broker's escrow account.
2: The broker has no authority to take the funds from the title company.
3: The broker cannot decide the dispute.

questions.q: A buyer under a contract with a financing contingency applies in good faith but is denied a loan. The broker holds the deposit. What may the broker do?
c: Return the deposit to the buyer without notifying the FREC
Notify the FREC within 15 business days and request an EDO
Hold the deposit until the seller signs a release
Give the deposit to the seller as liquidated damages
questions.ex: Under s. 475.25(1)(d)1, if the buyer in good faith fails to satisfy the financing clause, the licensee may return the deposit without notifying the commission or starting a settlement procedure. The same applies to a condo buyer cancelling under s. 718.503.

1: This is one of the statutory exceptions; no FREC notice is required.
2: The statute allows return to the buyer in this case.
3: A good-faith financing failure is not a buyer default.

questions.q: If the parties choose mediation for an escrow dispute, it must be completed within how many days after the last demand?
questions.ex: Mediation must be completed within 90 days after the last demand; otherwise the broker must promptly use another procedure.

0: 30 business days is the deadline to institute a procedure.

questions.q: An advertisement for a listed property that does not include the brokerage firm's registered name is a:
c: lawful ad if the associate's phone number appears
lawful ad if the property address appears
questions.ex: Omitting the registered brokerage name makes it a blind ad, in any medium.

2: The brokerage name is required regardless of other contact information.
3: The brokerage name is required whatever else the ad shows.

questions.q: A homeowner (not a licensee) posts her own house for sale on social media with her phone number. Must the ad include a brokerage name?
c: Yes, every real estate advertisement must include a brokerage name
No, an owner advertising her own property has no brokerage to name
Yes, unless the asking price is under $500,000, when owners are exempt
Only if she plans to pay a commission to a buyer's broker at closing
questions.ex: Advertising rules for brokerage names apply to licensees' ads. An owner selling her own property is exempt from licensure and there is no brokerage to name.

0: The rule applies to licensee advertising.
3: Paying a commission later does not change who placed this ad.

questions.q: A sales associate posts a listing video on her personal Instagram with her name and phone number, but not her brokerage's name. Which is correct?
c: Lawful because it is her personal account
Lawful if the brokerage name is in her profile page one click away
A blind ad; the registered brokerage name must appear in the ad
Lawful if the seller approved it
questions.ex: Licensee advertising on any medium must include the registered brokerage name. A personal account is not an exception.

0: Personal social media is still advertising by a licensee.
1: The firm name must appear in the ad itself.
3: Seller approval does not cure a blind ad.

questions.q: The entrance sign of a broker's office must include the broker's name, the trade name (if any), and the words:
c: 'Licensed Real Estate Broker' (or 'Lic. Real Estate Broker')
questions.ex: The sign must show the broker's name, any trade name, and 'Licensed Real Estate Broker' or 'Lic. Real Estate Broker'.

3: This is not the required wording.

questions.q: A seller is so happy with the sale that she hands the sales associate a $500 gift card at closing. Which is correct?
c: Lawful, because a voluntary gift after closing is not a commission
Lawful, as long as the gift is worth less than $1,000 and is disclosed
A violation: she may be compensated only by her employing broker
Lawful, if the gift card is disclosed on the closing statement
questions.ex: A sales associate may accept compensation for real estate services only from her employing broker.

0: Anything of value for services is compensation.
3: Disclosure does not fix the payment path.

questions.q: Which payment is lawful?
c: A broker pays an unlicensed assistant $100 for each closed transaction
A broker rebates part of the commission to the buyer, with full disclosure to all parties
A sales associate pays a referral fee directly to a licensee at another brokerage
A broker pays a past customer $300 for each new client referred
questions.ex: A broker may rebate part of the commission to a party to the transaction with disclosure. Payments to unlicensed persons for real estate services are unlawful; an associate cannot pay or receive compensation except through the broker.

0: Per-closing pay to an unlicensed person is compensation for real estate services.
2: Compensation must flow through the employing broker.
3: Paying unlicensed persons for referrals of business is not allowed.

questions.q: A prospective tenant paid $200 for a rental list but did not obtain a rental. She asks for a refund. How much must be returned (the list was accurate)?
questions.ex: If no rental is obtained, the tenant gets back any amount over 25% of the fee: 75% × $200 = $150. If the list was inaccurate, the full fee is refundable.

0: A refund is required when no rental is obtained.
1: $50 is the 25% the broker may keep.
3: The full fee is refundable only if the information was inaccurate.

questions.q: At a local association meeting, two brokers agree that neither will accept listings below 6%. This is:
c: price fixing, a violation of antitrust law
questions.ex: Commission rates must be negotiated between each broker and client. Agreements between competitors to set rates are price fixing.

0: A written agreement to fix prices is still illegal.
2: There is no lawful 'customary' or 'standard' rate.

questions.q: Which step comes immediately after the DBPR completes its investigation of a complaint?
c: The FREC issues a final order
A probable cause panel decides whether probable cause exists
The licensee appeals to the District Court of Appeal
A formal hearing before an administrative law judge
questions.ex: Complaint → investigation → probable cause determination → formal complaint → hearing → final order → appeal.

0: The final order comes after a hearing.
3: A formal hearing follows the formal complaint.

questions.q: A licensee disputes the facts in the formal complaint. Where is the case heard?
c: Informal hearing before the members of the FREC
Formal hearing before an administrative law judge
Trial before the Florida Supreme Court
Jury trial in the county court where he lives
questions.ex: Disputed facts go to a formal hearing before an administrative law judge, who issues a recommended order. Undisputed facts can be handled at an informal hearing before the FREC.

0: Informal hearings are for undisputed facts.
2: Appeals go to a District Court of Appeal.
3: County courts do not conduct license discipline hearings.

questions.q: A licensee may appeal an FREC final order to the District Court of Appeal within:
questions.ex: Appeal within 30 days of the final order.

questions.q: The maximum administrative fine the FREC may impose per violation is:
questions.ex: Up to $5,000 per violation (count).

questions.q: Performing real estate services for compensation without a license is a:
questions.ex: Operating without a valid, current, active license is a third-degree felony.

0: Most other s. 475.42 violations are second-degree misdemeanors.
1: Rental-list fraud (s. 475.453) has been a first-degree misdemeanor.

questions.q: A licensee repeatedly ignores escrow rules because 'deals always close anyway'. This reckless indifference is best described as:
questions.ex: Culpable negligence is reckless indifference to others' rights, more than a careless mistake.

0: Repeated, knowing disregard goes beyond simple negligence.
3: A false promise is a promise to induce action that the licensee does not intend or cannot keep.

questions.q: How long must a broker keep transaction records and escrow records?
questions.ex: At least 5 years (and at least 2 years after any related litigation ends).

0: 2 years relates to litigation, added after it ends.

questions.q: A licensee tells a buyer, 'The county will never allow anything to be built on that empty lot behind you,' knowing there is no such rule, to close the sale. This is best described as:
c: lawful sales talk to close the deal
questions.ex: Stating a false fact to induce a sale is misrepresentation; framed as an assurance about the future, it is a false promise. Puffing is exaggerated opinion ('best view in town').

0: Puffing is opinion, not a false statement of fact.
3: False statements of fact are violations.

questions.q: The maximum the Real Estate Recovery Fund will pay for claims arising from one transaction is:
questions.ex: $50,000 per transaction (all claimants combined); $150,000 aggregate against one licensee.

questions.q: A sales associate wins a judgment against her former broker for unpaid commissions but cannot collect. May she recover from the Fund?
c: Yes, up to $50,000, because the judgment arose from a real estate transaction
Yes, up to $150,000, the maximum the Fund pays against any one licensee
No; a licensee who acted as a licensee cannot recover for a commission dispute
Only if the broker has filed for bankruptcy and the judgment is discharged
questions.ex: The Fund protects the public. A licensee who acted as a licensee in the transaction (e.g., over a commission) cannot recover.

0: Commission disputes between licensees are excluded.
1: $150,000 is the per-licensee aggregate cap; she is excluded anyway.

questions.q: When the Fund pays a claim based on a judgment against a licensee, the licensee's license is:
c: revoked permanently, with no possibility of reinstatement
automatically suspended until the Fund is repaid with interest
unaffected, because the Fund exists to pay such judgments
placed on probation for 1 year while the licensee repays the Fund
questions.ex: Payment from the Fund automatically suspends the license until the licensee repays the full amount plus interest.

0: It is a suspension, not revocation.
3: Probation is not the automatic result.

questions.q: Which protected classes were added to the federal Fair Housing Act in 1988?
questions.ex: 1988 added familial status and handicap (disability). Sex was added in 1974.

0: Sex was added in 1974; religion was original (1968).
2: Age and marital status are ECOA classes.
3: Race and color were in the original 1968 act.

questions.q: A licensee shows a Hispanic buyer only homes in neighbourhoods where many Hispanic families live, although she did not ask for that. This is:
questions.ex: Steering is directing buyers toward or away from areas based on a protected class.

0: Blockbusting is scaring owners into selling.
1: Redlining is lender discrimination by area.

questions.q: An owner of three single-family homes sells one without a broker but runs an ad saying 'No children'. Which is correct?
c: Exempt, because he owns no more than three single-family homes
Not exempt: discriminatory advertising removes the exemption
Exempt because familial status is not protected
Exempt only if he lives in the house
questions.ex: The single-family owner exemption is lost if a broker is used or a discriminatory advertisement is published.

0: The exemption requires no broker AND no discriminatory advertising.
2: Familial status has been protected since 1988.
3: Owner occupancy is a condition of the Mrs. Murphy exemption, not this one.

questions.q: Which basis of discrimination has NO exemptions under federal law?
questions.ex: The Civil Rights Act of 1866 prohibits racial discrimination in all property transactions without exception.

0: Religious organizations have a limited exemption.
1: Housing for older persons is an exemption.

questions.q: A tenant who uses a wheelchair asks to install grab bars in the bathroom at her own expense. The landlord must generally allow this as a:
questions.ex: A physical change to the unit is a reasonable modification (generally at the tenant's expense). A change in rules or policies is an accommodation.

0: Accommodation is a change in rules or policies.
2: Nonconforming use is a zoning term.
3: A variance is a zoning term.

questions.q: A wheelchair ramp is required at a brokerage's office entrance. Which law governs?
questions.ex: The ADA governs accessibility of public accommodations and commercial facilities, such as a brokerage office.

0: The Fair Housing Act governs housing.

questions.q: Which call to a number on the National Do Not Call Registry is permitted?
c: Calling an expired listing of another brokerage
Calling a customer who closed a purchase with you 14 months ago
Calling someone who inquired about a listing 6 months ago
Calling a FSBO seller you have never met
questions.ex: An established business relationship lasts 18 months after a transaction and 3 months after an inquiry (FCC rule; since May 2024 the FTC rule uses roughly equivalent windows of 540 days and 90 days).

0: You have no business relationship with another brokerage's expired listing.
2: An inquiry creates a relationship for only 3 months.

questions.q: Under ECOA, a lender may NOT deny credit because the applicant:
c: has insufficient income to repay the loan
has a poor history of paying debts on time
lacks funds for the required down payment
questions.ex: ECOA prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age (if able to contract), receipt of public assistance income, or good-faith exercise of consumer credit rights.

0: Insufficient income is a legitimate credit factor.
2: Payment history is a legitimate factor.
3: Lack of funds is a legitimate factor.

questions.q: The Closing Disclosure must be received by the borrower at least how long before closing?
questions.ex: At least 3 business days before closing (consummation). The Loan Estimate is due within 3 business days of application.

3: 10 days is the lead-paint inspection window.

questions.q: A buyer closes on a purchase-money mortgage for her new home and wants to cancel the loan 2 days later. Which is correct?
c: She may rescind within 3 business days under TILA
She has no TILA right of rescission on a purchase loan
She may rescind only if the APR was disclosed late
questions.ex: TILA's 3-business-day right of rescission applies to refinances and home-equity loans on a principal residence, not to purchase loans.

0: Rescission applies to refinance/home-equity loans, not purchase loans.
3: Late disclosures do not create rescission for purchase loans.

questions.q: Which phrase in an advertisement is a TILA trigger term requiring full credit disclosure?
questions.ex: A specific down-payment amount is a trigger term. General phrases like 'easy financing' or 'low monthly payments' are not.

0: General statements are not trigger terms.
3: This is not a specific credit term.

questions.q: Under RESPA, a title company pays a sales associate $100 for every buyer she refers. This is:
c: lawful, as long as it is disclosed to the buyer in writing
a prohibited kickback for referral of settlement services
lawful, as long as the total stays under $500 per year
lawful, because title insurance is not a mortgage loan
questions.ex: RESPA prohibits kickbacks and unearned fees for referrals of settlement services in federally related residential transactions.

0: Chapter 475 talks about disclosure; RESPA prohibits the kickback outright.

questions.q: A landlord intends to keep part of a tenant's security deposit. Within how many days after the rental agreement ends must the landlord send written notice of the claim?
questions.ex: Return within 15 days if no claim; send notice of a claim within 30 days (by certified mail, or by e-mail if both parties signed the e-mail addendum, since July 1, 2025); the tenant has 15 days to object.

1: 15 days is the return deadline when no claim is made, and the tenant's objection window.

questions.q: Under current s. 83.57, how much written notice is required to end a month-to-month tenancy that has no specific term?
questions.ex: Current law: month-to-month and quarter-to-quarter 30 days; year-to-year 60 days; week-to-week 7 days. (Older texts said 15 days for month-to-month.)

1: 15 days is the pre-change rule found in older books.

questions.q: A landlord forgets to send the notice of claim and sends it 35 days after the rental agreement ended. What is the result?
c: The claim is still valid, because the damage to the unit is real
The landlord forfeits the right to impose a claim on the deposit
The landlord may keep half of the deposit as a late-notice penalty
The tenant must still object within 15 days or lose the deposit
questions.ex: A landlord who fails to give the 30-day notice forfeits the right to impose a claim on the deposit.

0: Missing the deadline forfeits the claim against the deposit.
3: The objection window matters only if the notice was timely.

questions.q: Which estate gives the greatest bundle of ownership rights?
questions.ex: Fee simple absolute is the most complete ownership: inheritable, unconditional, and of unlimited duration.

0: A life estate ends at death.
1: A defeasible fee can be lost if a condition occurs.
3: An estate for years is a leasehold, not ownership.

questions.q: Ana deeds her house 'to Bruno for life, then to Carla.' Bruno dies. Who owns the house?
questions.ex: When the future interest goes to a third party it is a remainder; Carla is the remainderman. If it returned to Ana it would be a reversion.

0: Reversion applies when no remainderman is named.
1: A life estate cannot be inherited; it ends at Bruno's death.
3: Escheat applies only when no heirs or will exist.

questions.q: A life tenant cuts down all the valuable timber on the property and sells it. This is:
questions.ex: A life tenant must not commit waste — actions that permanently damage the value of the future interest.

0: The life tenant may use but not destroy the property's value.
2: Adverse possession is acquiring another's land.
3: An easement is a right of use.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the rights in the bundle of rights?
questions.ex: The bundle: possession, control, enjoyment, exclusion, disposition. Escheat is a government power over property of owners who die without will or heirs.

questions.q: A lease for 6 months with a definite end date is classified as:
questions.ex: Any lease with a definite beginning and end, even shorter than a year, is an estate for years. It ends automatically without notice.

1: A tenancy at will has no fixed term.
2: A periodic tenancy renews period to period.
3: Sufferance is a holdover without consent.

questions.q: With 14 months left on her 3-year lease, a tenant transfers all 14 remaining months to a friend, who pays the landlord directly. This is:
questions.ex: Transferring the entire remaining term is an assignment, even if it is only part of the original term.

0: A sublease transfers only part of what remains.
2: A novation would release the original tenant by agreement with the landlord; nothing says that happened.

questions.q: A retail store pays base rent plus 4% of gross sales over $500,000. This is a:
questions.ex: Rent based on a percentage of the tenant's gross sales is a percentage lease, common in retail.

0: A gross lease has fixed rent with the landlord paying expenses.
1: A net lease shifts property expenses to the tenant.
3: A graduated lease has scheduled rent increases.

questions.q: A commercial tenant pays rent plus property taxes, insurance and maintenance. This is a:
questions.ex: Triple net: the tenant pays taxes, insurance and maintenance in addition to rent.

0: In a gross lease the landlord pays those expenses.
2: A graduated lease has scheduled rent increases.
3: An index lease ties rent to an index such as CPI.

questions.q: Two unmarried friends receive a deed that says nothing about how they hold title. In Florida they own as:
c: joint tenants with right of survivorship
questions.ex: Florida presumes tenancy in common for unmarried co-owners unless survivorship is expressly stated.

0: Florida requires express survivorship language for joint tenancy.
3: Florida is not a community-property state.

questions.q: Ana and Rui own a duplex as tenants in common, 60%/40%. Rui dies with a will leaving everything to his sister. Who owns Rui's 40%?
questions.ex: A tenant in common's share passes by will or to heirs; there is no survivorship.

0: Survivorship belongs to joint tenancy and entireties, not tenancy in common.
2: Escheat applies only without a will or heirs.

questions.q: The four unities required for a joint tenancy are:
questions.ex: PITT: Possession, Interest, Time, Title.

1: Income and tax are not unities.
3: Insurance and transfer are not unities.

questions.q: A creditor obtains a judgment against the husband alone. The couple owns their condo as tenants by the entireties. Can the creditor force a sale of the condo to satisfy the husband's debt?
c: Yes, by forcing a sale of the husband's half of the condo
Yes, by forcing a sale of the entire condo to pay the debt
No, entireties property is shielded from one spouse's individual creditors
Only after the wife dies and the husband becomes the sole owner of the condo
questions.ex: Tenancy by the entireties property is protected from the creditors of only one spouse.

0: Neither spouse holds a separate half.
1: Individual creditors cannot reach entireties property.
3: If the wife dies first, she owns it alone by survivorship and the husband's creditor still cannot reach it.

questions.q: Florida's constitutional homestead protection inside a municipality covers up to:
questions.ex: 1/2 acre of contiguous land within a municipality; 160 contiguous acres outside a municipality.

questions.q: Which claim can result in a forced sale of a Florida homestead?
questions.ex: Homestead protection does not stop property taxes and assessments, the mortgage on the home, or liens for work on the home.

0: General creditors cannot force the sale of homestead.
1: General creditors cannot force the sale of homestead.
3: General creditors cannot force the sale of homestead.

questions.q: A married homeowner holds title to the homestead in his name only and wants to mortgage it. What is required?
c: Only his signature, because title is in his name
His spouse must join in the mortgage
Nothing, if the loan is under $100,000
questions.ex: When the owner is married, the spouse must join in any conveyance or mortgage of the homestead (manual statement; not yet verified against the constitution's text).

0: Homestead rules require spousal joinder regardless of title.
2: Court approval is not the requirement.

questions.q: The buyer of a cooperative apartment receives:
c: shares in the corporation and a proprietary lease
an undivided interest in common elements only
questions.ex: In a cooperative, the corporation owns the building. The buyer receives shares and a proprietary lease, which is personal property.

0: A deed to a unit is a condominium purchase.
3: Common elements belong to condominium ownership.

questions.q: A buyer signs a contract to buy a new condominium unit from the developer. The buyer may cancel within:
questions.ex: Developer sales: 15 days after signing and receiving the required documents. Resales: 7 days excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays (since July 1, 2025; older books say 3 business days). Timeshares: 10 days.

0: 7 days (excluding weekends and holidays) is the resale rule.

questions.q: A timeshare purchaser's statutory cancellation period is:
questions.ex: Until midnight of the 10th calendar day after the later of signing the contract or receiving the last required document; the right cannot be waived (s. 721.10).

3: 15 days is the developer condo rule.

questions.q: A condominium is legally created by:
c: filing articles of incorporation for the association
the first sale of a unit
questions.ex: Recording the declaration of condominium creates the condominium.

1: The association is created separately; the declaration creates the condominium.
2: A CO allows occupancy of a building.

questions.q: In Florida, adverse possession requires open, notorious, hostile and continuous possession for:
c: 5 years, plus a recorded claim of ownership
7 years, plus color of title or payment of taxes
20 years of possession, with no other condition
10 years, plus a survey filed with the county
questions.ex: Florida: 7 years plus either color of title or payment of property taxes. 20 years is the prescriptive easement period.

0: It is 7 years plus color of title or payment of taxes.
2: 20 years is for an easement by prescription.
3: It is 7 years and an additional condition applies.

questions.q: A person dies without a will and without heirs. The property passes to the state by:
questions.ex: Escheat transfers property to the state when there is no will and no heirs.

0: Eminent domain is a taking with compensation.
2: Adverse possession requires possession by a claimant.
3: Devise is a gift of real property by will.

questions.q: Real property left to a person in a will is called a:
questions.ex: A devise is a gift of real property by will; the recipient is the devisee.

0: A bequest is a gift of personal property.
2: Descent is transfer without a will.

questions.q: Which deed gives the buyer the most protection?
questions.ex: A general warranty deed warrants title against defects from any time, even before the grantor owned the property.

1: Special warranty covers only the grantor's period of ownership.
3: Bargain and sale implies ownership but gives no warranties.

questions.q: Which is required for a deed to be valid in Florida?
c: The grantee's signature on the deed at closing
Recording in the county's official public records
Delivery and acceptance during the grantor's lifetime
A notary's acknowledgment of the grantor's signature
questions.ex: A valid deed needs a competent grantor, an identifiable grantee, consideration, words of conveyance, a legal description, the grantor's signature with two witnesses, and delivery and acceptance. Recording and acknowledgment protect against third parties; the grantee does not sign.

0: The grantee does not sign the deed.
1: Recording gives constructive notice; it is not needed for validity.
3: Acknowledgment is needed to record, not for validity.

questions.q: To remove an ex-spouse's possible claim from a title, the ex-spouse would most likely sign a:
questions.ex: A quitclaim conveys whatever interest the grantor may have, without warranties — the standard tool to cure a cloud on title.

0: The ex-spouse would not warrant the entire title.
2: Warranties are unnecessary to release a claim.
3: A deed of trust is a security instrument.

questions.q: How many witnesses must sign a Florida deed with the grantor?
questions.ex: The grantor signs in the presence of two subscribing witnesses (s. 689.01). Leases no longer require witnesses.

0: No witnesses is the current rule for leases, not deeds.

questions.q: A buyer fails to check the public records and later claims she did not know of a recorded easement. Which is correct?
c: She is not bound because she had no actual notice
She is bound because recording gives constructive notice
She is bound only if the seller told her
questions.ex: Recorded documents give constructive notice to everyone, whether or not they read them.

0: Constructive notice applies regardless of actual knowledge.
3: A recorded easement does not void the sale.

questions.q: An owner's title insurance policy protects the owner against:
c: liens and judgments the owner allows to attach after closing
undiscovered defects that existed before the policy date
zoning changes that reduce the property's value after closing
physical damage to the home from hurricanes and flooding
questions.ex: Title insurance covers defects existing before the policy date. It does not cover problems the owner creates later or physical damage.

2: Zoning changes are not title defects.

questions.q: A property is foreclosed. It has a first mortgage recorded in 2010, a judgment lien recorded in 2018, and unpaid property taxes for last year. Which is paid first from the sale?
questions.ex: Property tax and special assessment liens have priority over other liens regardless of recording date. Others follow recording order.

0: Taxes come before even an older first mortgage.
1: A judgment lien is behind taxes and earlier-recorded liens.
3: Liens are paid in priority order.

questions.q: A power company's right to run lines across a property is an easement:
questions.ex: An easement in gross benefits a person or company, not an adjoining parcel; there is no dominant estate.

0: Appurtenant easements benefit a neighbouring parcel.
2: Easements by necessity arise for landlocked parcels.
3: Prescription is acquired by long adverse use.

questions.q: In Florida an easement by prescription requires continuous, open, adverse use for:
questions.ex: 20 years for a prescriptive easement; 7 years (with color of title or taxes) for adverse possession of title.

questions.q: A neighbour's fence extends 2 feet onto your client's lot. This is an:
questions.ex: An encroachment is a physical intrusion onto another's land, typically revealed by a survey.

0: An easement is a right to use land.
3: An appurtenance is a right attached to land.

questions.q: Which is a general lien?
questions.ex: A judgment lien attaches to all the debtor's property in the county where recorded — a general lien. The others are specific liens on one property.

0: A mortgage is a specific lien.
1: A property tax lien is specific to that parcel.
3: A construction lien is specific to the improved property.

questions.q: A restaurant tenant bolted its pizza ovens to the floor. Before the lease ends, the landlord sells the building. Who owns the ovens?
c: The landlord, because the ovens are bolted to the floor
The building buyer, because fixtures pass with the deed
The tenant, as trade fixtures removed by the end of the lease
The county, as unclaimed property after the lease ends
questions.ex: Trade fixtures installed by a business tenant remain the tenant's personal property and must be removed by the end of the lease.

school taxes only, on assessed value between $50,000 and $75,000
only owners aged 65 or older with limited household income
questions.ex: First exemption: $25,000 off all taxes. Second: up to $25,000 (indexed to CPI since 2025) off non-school taxes on value above $50,000.

2: The second exemption excludes school taxes.
3: Age is not a requirement for these exemptions.

questions.q: The property tax exemption for a widow, widower, blind person, or totally and permanently disabled person is currently:
questions.ex: $5,000 (raised from $500 by the 2022 Legislature, effective for the 2023 tax roll).

0: $500 is the old amount in older books.

questions.q: A homestead is assessed at $280,000. School millage is 5.5 mills and non-school millage is 8.2 mills. Using $25,000 for each homestead exemption, what is the total tax?
questions.ex: 1 mill = 0.001. The second exemption does not reduce school taxes.

questions.q: A homestead's assessed value last year was $200,000. Market value rose 9% and the CPI rose 4.1%. Under Save Our Homes, what is the maximum assessed value this year?
Residential rental buildings are depreciated for income tax purposes over:
questions.ex: 27.5 years for residential rental; 39 years for nonresidential. Land is never depreciated.

questions.q: An investor bought a rental for $250,000, added $40,000 of improvements, and took $60,000 of depreciation. She sells for a net $400,000. What is her taxable gain?
questions.ex: Depreciation lowers basis and raises the gain.

questions.q: In a 1031 exchange of investment property, the investor also receives $20,000 in cash. What is the effect?
c: The whole exchange becomes taxable, because cash is not like-kind property
The $20,000 is taxable boot; the rest of the exchange stays tax-deferred
Nothing is taxable, because the properties exchanged were like-kind
The exchange is void, and the investor must reverse both transfers
questions.ex: Boot (cash, debt relief, non-like-kind property) is taxable, but it does not disqualify the exchange.

0: Boot does not disqualify the exchange.
2: Boot is taxable to the extent of gain.

questions.q: A married couple filing jointly sells the home they lived in for the last 4 years. How much gain can they generally exclude?
questions.ex: $500,000 married filing jointly ($250,000 single) if owned and used as the main home 2 of the last 5 years.

questions.q: An owner's lot is unusually narrow, so a house cannot meet the side setback. She asks to build 3 feet closer to the line. She is requesting a:
questions.ex: A variance permits deviation from a dimensional requirement because of a hardship unique to the parcel.

0: A special exception is a use permitted with approval.
3: A nonconforming use predates the zoning rule.

questions.q: A county adopts zoning that limits building height. Owners receive no compensation. The county is using:
questions.ex: Zoning and building codes are police power — regulation for health, safety and welfare without compensation. Eminent domain is a taking with just compensation.

2: Escheat concerns owners with no heirs.

questions.q: A store operating legally before the area was rezoned residential may continue to operate. This is a:
questions.ex: A nonconforming ('grandfathered') use may continue but typically cannot expand, and may be lost if destroyed or abandoned.

0: A variance is relief from a dimensional rule.
2: A special exception is a permitted use with approval.
3: A PUD is a planned development.

questions.q: Before a new building may be occupied, the owner must obtain a:
questions.ex: A certificate of occupancy is issued after final inspection; the building permit is needed before construction.

2: A variance is not required for occupancy.
3: A plan amendment is not required to occupy a building.

questions.q: Under federal lead-based paint rules, a buyer of pre-1978 housing generally has how many days to conduct a lead inspection (unless waived)?
questions.ex: 10 days, which the buyer may waive. Sellers must also disclose known hazards and provide the EPA pamphlet.

3: 15 days is the developer condo cancellation period.

questions.q: A new owner discovers buried industrial waste left by a prior owner. Under CERCLA, the new owner:
c: cannot be liable, because she did not cause the contamination herself
can be liable unless she qualifies for a defense, such as innocent landowner
is liable only if she knew about the buried waste before she bought
can sue the state for compensation, because the waste predates her
questions.ex: CERCLA liability is strict, joint and several; current owners can be liable. The innocent-landowner defense requires appropriate due diligence (e.g., a Phase I environmental audit) before purchase.

0: Liability does not depend on causing the contamination.

questions.q: Asbestos insulation that is intact and not crumbling is often best handled by:
questions.ex: Asbestos is dangerous when friable (crumbling); encapsulation is often safer than removal.

0: Removal can release fibers and requires licensed abatement.

questions.q: A sales associate wants to work for two unrelated brokerages at the same time to earn more. Which is correct?
c: Allowed, if both brokers sign a written consent
Not allowed: a sales associate may work for only one employer at a time
Allowed, if she holds a separate license for each brokerage
Allowed for up to 90 days while she chooses one brokerage
questions.ex: A sales associate may hold only one license and be registered with only one employing broker (or owner-developer) at a time. Only brokers may hold multiple licenses.

0: Consent cannot create a second employer.
2: Multiple licenses are available only to brokers.

questions.q: Which sale is a 'residential sale' for brokerage disclosure purposes?
questions.ex: Residential sale: improved residential property of ≤4 units, unimproved residential land for ≤4 units, or agricultural property of ≤10 acres.

3: Agricultural property counts only up to 10 acres.

questions.q: Under CAN-SPAM, a brokerage must honor an email recipient's opt-out request within:
questions.ex: Opt-out requests must be honored within 10 business days; commercial emails also need truthful headers and a physical postal address.

1: 3 business days is a TRID/TILA number.

questions.q: A Florida landlord receives a tenant's security deposit. Within how many days must the landlord notify the tenant in writing how the deposit is being held?
questions.ex: In the lease or within 30 days of receipt, the landlord discloses in writing where the deposit is held (or that a surety bond was posted) and whether interest is paid (s. 83.49(2)). Landlords who rent fewer than 5 units are exempt.

1: 15 days is the return deadline at move-out when no claim is made.
3: 60 days is the year-to-year termination notice.

questions.q: When must a buyer in a community with a mandatory homeowners' association receive the HOA disclosure summary?
c: Before the buyer signs the sale contract
At closing, with the other HOA documents
Within 30 days after the closing date
Only if the buyer asks for it in writing
questions.ex: The HOA disclosure summary must be provided before the contract is executed. If it was not, the buyer may void the contract within 3 days after receiving it or before closing, whichever occurs first; the right cannot be waived and ends at closing (s. 720.401).

1: Closing is too late; the disclosure comes before contract.

questions.q: Which event does NOT terminate a listing agreement?
c: The seller dies before a buyer is found
The listed house is destroyed by a fire
The listing period expires with no sale
The listing associate moves to another firm
questions.ex: The listing is a contract between the seller and the brokerage, not the individual associate, so it stays with the brokerage. Death, destruction and expiration all end it.

0: Death of a party ends a personal-service contract.
1: Destruction of the property ends the listing.

questions.q: A seller signs an AS IS contract. He knows the pool leaks underground but says nothing; the leak is not visible. After closing the buyer discovers it. Which is correct?
c: The buyer has no claim, because AS IS means the buyer accepted the leak
The seller may be liable for failing to disclose a known latent material defect
The buyer has no claim, because the inspection period has ended
Only the listing broker can be liable, never the seller
questions.ex: Under Johnson v. Davis, a seller must disclose known facts materially affecting value that are not readily observable. AS IS limits repair obligations; it does not excuse concealment.

0: AS IS does not cover concealed defects the seller knew about.
2: The duty to disclose is separate from the inspection period.
3: The seller's own duty exists; licensees may also be liable.

questions.q: Under the course's benchmarks, an FHA borrower's housing and total obligations ratios should not exceed:
questions.ex: Course convention: FHA 31% / 43%; conventional 28% / 36%. These are teaching benchmarks, not statutes.

questions.q: A sales associate's 14 hours of continuing education each renewal period must consist of:
c: 3 hours Core Law, 3 hours Ethics and Business Practices, 8 hours specialty
14 hours of any FREC-approved courses, chosen freely by the licensee
3 hours Core Law and 11 hours of specialty education of any kind
7 hours Core Law and 7 hours Ethics and Business Practices courses
questions.ex: The 14 hours are split 3 Core Law + 3 Ethics and Business Practices + 8 specialty (mandatory for licenses expiring on or after March 31, 2025).

1: The hours are split into required categories.
2: 3 of the hours must be Ethics and Business Practices.
3: Core Law and Ethics are 3 hours each.

questions.q: Under the FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule as amended in 2024, an established business relationship based on a consumer's inquiry lasts:
questions.ex: FTC rule (since May 16, 2024): 540 days after a transaction, 90 days after an inquiry. The FCC rule still states 18 months and 3 months.

2: 540 days is the window after a purchase or transaction.
3: 18 months is the FCC transaction window.

questions.q: A Tampa landlord is about to sign a 12-month residential lease. Under Florida law since October 2025, the landlord must:
c: give the statutory flood disclosure at or before signing the lease
give a flood disclosure only if the unit is in a FEMA flood zone
deliver a flood disclosure within 30 days after the tenant moves in
do nothing, because flood disclosures apply only to sales of homes
questions.ex: s. 83.512: for a residential lease of 1 year or longer, the landlord gives the flood disclosure (a separate statutory form) at or before signing.

1: The duty does not depend on the flood zone.
2: It is due at or before signing.
3: Since October 2025 it also applies to leases of 1 year or more.

questions.q: Which of these residential rentals requires the landlord's flood disclosure under s. 83.512?
questions.ex: The disclosure applies to rental agreements for a term of 1 year or longer. Shorter terms are not covered.

0: The threshold is a term of 1 year or longer.
2: A month-to-month tenancy is not a 1-year term.

questions.q: A buyer signs a contract for a resale condominium unit and receives the association documents the same day. The contract has the statutory cancellation clause. Under current Florida law, the buyer may cancel by written notice within:
c: 3 days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays
7 days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays
10 calendar days, including weekends and legal holidays
15 days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays
questions.ex: Since July 1, 2025 (ch. 2025-175), the resale period is 7 days excluding weekends and legal holidays, after signing and receiving the documents. Older books say 3 business days. Developer sales: 15 days. Timeshares: 10 days.

0: 3 days is the pre-2025 resale rule found in older books.
2: 10 calendar days is the timeshare rule.
3: 15 days is the developer sale rule.

questions.q: A buyer of a home in a mandatory HOA community did not receive the HOA disclosure summary before signing. The summary arrives 10 days before closing. The buyer may void the contract:
c: within 3 days after receiving the summary, but not after closing
at any time before closing, because the summary arrived late
within 15 days after receiving the summary, as in a developer sale
only if the seller agrees in writing to release the buyer from it
questions.ex: s. 720.401: within 3 days after receiving the summary or before closing, whichever occurs first. Here the 3-day window ends first.

1: The right ends 3 days after receipt or at closing, whichever comes first.
2: 15 days is the developer condominium rule.
3: The statutory right does not need the seller's consent.

flashcards.f: Statute vs administrative rule: what is the difference, with one Florida real estate example of each?
flashcards.b: A statute is passed by the Legislature (Chapter 475 F.S., the license law). A rule is adopted by an agency under a statute's authority (Rule 61J2 F.A.C., e.g., escrow deposit deadlines adopted by FREC).

flashcards.f: DBPR vs FREC — who investigates, who disciplines, who issues licenses?
flashcards.b: DBPR issues licenses and investigates complaints. FREC adopts rules and disciplines (final orders). Courts handle crimes and civil damages.

flashcards.f: The three elements that require a real estate license.
flashcards.b: A real estate service, for another, for compensation (paid, promised or expected).

flashcards.f: A builder's salaried employee sells the builder's homes. Then she's paid per closing. License needed?
flashcards.b: Salaried only: exempt. Paid per closing: license required — the exemption depends on no commission/transaction-based pay.

flashcards.f: Mutual recognition: who can use it, and what exam do they take?
flashcards.b: Only applicants who are NOT Florida residents when they apply, licensed in a state with an agreement. They take a 40-question Florida law exam and need 30 correct.

flashcards.f: Missed post-license education vs missed continuing education: consequences?
flashcards.b: Post-license (45 hrs) missed before first renewal → license null and void. CE (14 hrs) missed at a later renewal → involuntary inactive (recoverable for 2 years).

flashcards.f: Involuntary inactive for 18 months. What does reactivation require?
flashcards.b: The 28-hour commission-prescribed reactivation course (more than 12 but less than 24 months). ≤12 months: 14 hours. >24 months: license expired.

flashcards.f: What event starts a 10-day clock and what event starts a 30-day clock for a licensee's duty to notify DBPR?
flashcards.b: 10 days: change of mailing or e-mail address (also a change of employing broker). 30 days: conviction, finding of guilt, or guilty or nolo contendere plea to any crime.
Group license: a sales associate (or broker associate) works for several CONNECTED entities of one owner-developer. Multiple licenses: a BROKER holds separate licenses for unconnected brokerages.
Transaction broker (unless single agent or no brokerage relationship is established in writing).

flashcards.f: Name the four duties owed ONLY by a single agent.
flashcards.b: Loyalty, obedience, (full) confidentiality, full disclosure.

flashcards.f: Transaction-broker duty not to reveal that the seller will take less, the buyer will pay more, a party's motivation, or facts a party asks to keep confidential.
flashcards.b: Limited confidentiality.

flashcards.f: When must the No Brokerage Relationship Notice be given?
flashcards.b: Before showing the property.

flashcards.f: When must the Single Agent Notice be given?
flashcards.b: Before or at the time of entering into a listing or representation agreement, or before showing property — whichever comes first.

flashcards.f: List four situations where brokerage disclosure is NOT required.
flashcards.b: Any four of: party already represented; bona fide open house/model showing; unanticipated casual encounter; general factual questions about advertised property; general info about qualifications/firm; auctions; appraisals; leases without an option to buy ≤4 units; nonresidential/commercial; business enterprises (except ≤4 residential units).

flashcards.f: Latent defect vs stigma: which must be disclosed in Florida?
flashcards.b: Known latent material defects (hidden roof leak, flooding) must be disclosed. Death on the property and HIV/AIDS status are declared not material.

flashcards.f: Which duties survive termination of a brokerage relationship?
flashcards.b: Confidentiality and accounting for funds.

flashcards.f: Deposit received Wednesday (no holidays). Associate's deadline? Broker's deadline?
flashcards.b: Associate → broker: end of Thursday (next business day). Broker deposits: end of Monday (Thu 1, Fri 2, Mon 3).
Commingling: mixing personal and escrow funds. Conversion: using escrow funds for personal or unauthorized purposes (more serious).
Mediation (all consent, 90 days), Arbitration (all consent, binding), Litigation (interpleader), Escrow disbursement order from FREC (only if the broker holds the funds).

flashcards.f: Two statutory situations where a broker may return a deposit to the buyer without notifying FREC.
flashcards.b: A residential condo buyer cancels under s. 718.503; the buyer in good faith fails to satisfy the contract's financing clause.

flashcards.f: An ad by a licensee that omits the registered brokerage name.
flashcards.b: Blind ad.

flashcards.f: Who may pay a sales associate for real estate services?
flashcards.b: Only the sales associate's employing broker (or owner-developer employer).

flashcards.f: Put in order: final order, probable cause, investigation, formal complaint, hearing, complaint, appeal.
flashcards.b: Complaint → investigation → probable cause → formal complaint → hearing → final order → appeal (30 days).
Misrepresentation: a false statement (or concealment) of material fact. Culpable negligence: reckless indifference to others' rights — beyond simple carelessness, without intent to deceive.

flashcards.f: Who cannot recover from the Real Estate Recovery Fund?
flashcards.b: A licensee who acted as a licensee in the transaction (e.g., commission disputes); also excluded: amounts above caps, treble damages, court costs, attorney's fees, interest.

Steering: guiding buyers toward/away from areas by protected class. Blockbusting: scaring owners into selling because a protected class is moving in. Redlining: lender refusing or varying loans by area.
Modification: physical change to the unit (usually tenant pays). Accommodation: change in rules/policies (e.g., service animal despite no-pets rule).

flashcards.f: TILA's 3-business-day right of rescission applies to which loans?
flashcards.b: Refinances and home-equity loans on the borrower's principal residence — not purchase loans, not investment property.

flashcards.f: Match: housing / credit / public accommodations / lending data.
flashcards.b: Fair Housing Act / ECOA / ADA / HMDA.

flashcards.f: Security deposit timeline after the tenant moves out.
flashcards.b: 15 days to return if no claim; certified-mail notice of claim within 30 days; tenant has 15 days to object. Missing the 30-day notice forfeits the claim.
Remainder: future interest goes to a third party (remainderman). Reversion: it returns to the grantor or heirs.

Assignment: the ENTIRE remaining term; assignee pays landlord; original tenant secondarily liable unless released. Sublease: part of the term or space; subtenant pays tenant; tenant stays primarily liable.

flashcards.f: Married couple, deed silent. Unmarried pair, deed silent. How is title held in each case?
flashcards.b: Married: tenancy by the entireties. Unmarried: tenancy in common.

flashcards.f: Florida homestead: name the three separate legal effects.
flashcards.b: (1) Protection from forced sale by most creditors; (2) restrictions on transfer and devise when there is a spouse/minor child (spouse joins deeds and mortgages); (3) property-tax exemption.
Condo: deed to a unit (real property) + undivided share of common elements. Co-op: shares in the corporation + proprietary lease (personal property).

flashcards.f: General warranty vs special warranty deed.
flashcards.b: General: grantor warrants against defects from any time. Special: only defects arising during the grantor's ownership.

flashcards.f: What makes a Florida deed valid, and what is needed only for recording?
flashcards.b: Valid: writing, competent grantor, identifiable grantee, consideration, words of conveyance, legal description, grantor's signature + 2 witnesses, delivery and acceptance. Recording: notary acknowledgment.

flashcards.f: Easement appurtenant vs easement in gross.
flashcards.b: Appurtenant: benefits an adjacent parcel (dominant/servient), runs with the land. In gross: benefits a person or company (utility), no dominant estate.

flashcards.f: Adverse possession vs easement by prescription (Florida periods).
flashcards.b: Adverse possession (title): 7 years + color of title or payment of taxes. Prescription (easement): 20 years of adverse use.
Accretion: gradual deposit of soil — owner gains land, boundary moves. Avulsion: sudden change — boundary does not move.

flashcards.f: Four tests for whether an item is a fixture.
flashcards.b: Intent (most important), method of annexation, adaptation to the property, relationship of the parties. Trade fixtures stay the tenant's.
640 ÷ (product of the denominators). Use AND to add separate parcels.

flashcards.f: Where is section 1, section 6, section 31, section 36?
flashcards.b: 1 = NE corner; 6 = NW; 31 = SW; 36 = SE (serpentine numbering from the NE).
Part = Total × Rate; Total = Part ÷ Rate; Rate = Part ÷ Total.
(New − Old) ÷ Old. The base is always the starting value.

flashcards.f: Sale price needed to net the seller a given amount.
flashcards.b: Price = (Net + fixed costs) ÷ (1 − commission rate). Never multiply the net by (1 + rate).

flashcards.f: Recover the original cost from a sale price and profit %.
flashcards.b: Cost = Sale ÷ (1 + profit%). For a loss: Cost = Sale ÷ (1 − loss%).
LTV = loan ÷ lesser of sale price or appraised value.

flashcards.f: First month's interest on an amortized loan.
flashcards.b: Balance × annual rate ÷ 12. Principal = payment − interest.

flashcards.f: Deed stamps, note stamps, intangible tax — formulas and who customarily pays.
flashcards.b: Deed: round price UP to $100 → ÷100 × $0.70 (seller). Note: round loan UP → ÷100 × $0.35 (buyer; new and assumed). Intangible: new loan × 0.002 (buyer).

flashcards.f: Proration of unpaid property taxes: which party is debited?
flashcards.b: Debit seller, credit buyer (taxes paid in arrears).

flashcards.f: Proration of rent collected in advance by the seller: which party is credited?
flashcards.b: Credit buyer, debit seller, for the buyer's days (including the closing day).

flashcards.f: Single or double entry? Binder deposit; new mortgage; assumed mortgage; seller's payoff.
flashcards.b: Deposit: credit buyer (single). New mortgage: credit buyer (single). Assumed mortgage: debit seller + credit buyer (double). Payoff: debit seller (single).

flashcards.f: Housing ratio and total obligations ratio.
flashcards.b: Housing = PITI ÷ gross monthly income. Total = (PITI + recurring debts) ÷ gross monthly income. Course benchmarks: 28/36 conventional; 31/43 FHA.

flashcards.f: IRV and how to build NOI.
flashcards.b: Value = NOI ÷ cap rate. NOI = PGI − vacancy & collection loss − operating expenses (NOT debt service or depreciation).
GRM = price ÷ MONTHLY gross rent (1–4 units). GIM = price ÷ ANNUAL gross income.
Value = land value + (cost new − accrued depreciation).
Adjust the comparable, never the subject. Comparable better → subtract; comparable inferior → add (CBS / CIA).
School tax = (assessed − 25,000) × school mills ÷ 1,000. Non-school = (assessed − 50,000*) × other mills ÷ 1,000. (*second exemption is up to $25,000, CPI-indexed since 2025.)
Cash flow = NOI − debt service. Cap rate = NOI ÷ price.
Assumption: buyer becomes personally liable (seller stays secondarily liable unless novation). Subject to: buyer pays but has no personal liability.

flashcards.f: FHA vs VA: role and borrower charge.
flashcards.b: FHA insures (borrower pays MIP). VA guarantees (borrower pays funding fee). Neither lends.
Primary: originates loans (banks, credit unions, mortgage bankers/brokers). Secondary: buys existing loans (Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac; Ginnie Mae guarantees FHA/VA securities).
Void: no contract at all. Voidable: one party may cancel (minor, fraud, duress). Unenforceable: valid but a court won't enforce (no required writing, time-barred).

flashcards.f: Exclusive right of sale vs exclusive agency: owner sells to her neighbour herself.
flashcards.b: Exclusive right of sale: commission owed. Exclusive agency: no commission.

flashcards.f: Effect of a counteroffer on the original offer.
flashcards.b: It rejects and terminates the original offer permanently.
Variance: deviation from a dimensional rule due to hardship unique to the parcel. Special exception: a use the code allows with case-by-case approval.
Police power: regulation (zoning, codes), no compensation. Eminent domain: taking for public use, just compensation required.
1031: investment/business real property exchanged for like-kind; gain deferred; boot taxable. Residence: exclude $250k/$500k gain if owned and used 2 of last 5 years.

flashcards.f: Pre-license course (sales associate) — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
63 hours (50-minute hours), including the end-of-course exam
Conditions: The course completion becomes invalid if the state exam is not PASSED within 2 years after completing the course (V-31).
Qualifications: Mutual-recognition nonresidents skip the course (see N-007).

flashcards.f: Applicant minimum age / education — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
18 years old; high school diploma or equivalent; U.S. Social Security number
Qualifications: U.S. citizenship and Florida residency are NOT required. Florida Bar members are exempt from the pre-license course (V-31).

flashcards.f: State exam passing score — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
75 correct out of 100 (75%)
Qualifications: Mutual recognition law exam: 30 of 40 (N-007).

flashcards.f: Exam time limit — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: 3.5 hours

flashcards.f: Application validity — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: Expires 2 years after DBPR receives it if the applicant has not passed the exam

flashcards.f: Reapplying after denial for dishonesty — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: May reapply after 2 years (manual statement)

flashcards.f: Mutual recognition law exam — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
40 questions; 30 correct to pass (75%)
Conditions: Must hold an active license in good standing in that state.
Qualifications: Florida residents cannot use mutual recognition. The other state's license must have been earned by its own course and exam. Current states (9): AL, AR, CT, GA, KY, MS, NE, RI, WV; Illinois ended Dec 31, 2025 (V-22).

flashcards.f: Post-license education (sales associate) — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
45 hours, completed before the FIRST renewal
Qualifications: Missing it makes the license NULL AND VOID; must requalify (63-hour course and state exam). Exempt: 4-year degree in real estate. Attorneys are NOT exempt. FREC may allow 6 more months for physical hardship.

flashcards.f: Continuing education — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
14 hours per 2-year renewal period (after the first renewal): 3 hours Core Law + 3 hours Ethics and Business Practices + 8 hours specialty
Conditions: Applies to active and voluntary-inactive licensees.
Qualifications: Missing renewal → involuntary inactive (not void). Florida Bar members are exempt from CE.

flashcards.f: First renewal timing — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
18–24 months after initial licensure
Conditions: Later renewal periods are 24 months.

flashcards.f: Reactivation from involuntary inactive — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
≤12 months: 14 hours CE. More than 12 but less than 24 months: 28-hour reactivation course. More than 24 months: license expires (null and void).
Qualifications: Voluntary inactive can be renewed indefinitely with 14 hours CE per cycle.

flashcards.f: Change of mailing or e-mail address — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: Notify DBPR in writing within 10 days

flashcards.f: Reporting a crime (conviction, finding of guilt or plea) — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
Within 30 days, in writing, including pleas of guilty or nolo contendere, to any crime in any jurisdiction
Conditions: Applies whether or not adjudication is withheld.

flashcards.f: Broker license prerequisites — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
24 months active sales associate license during the preceding 5 years; 72-hour broker course; broker exam
Conditions: Alternatives to the 24 months as a sales associate: salaried government employee holding a sales associate license, or broker licensed in another jurisdiction (same 24 months in 5 years). Sales associate post-licensing must be complete.

flashcards.f: Broker post-license education — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
60 hours (two 30-hour courses) before first broker renewal
Qualifications: Missing it voids the broker license.

flashcards.f: FREC membership — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: 7 members: 4 brokers (active 5 preceding years), 1 broker or sales associate (active 2 preceding years), 2 consumer members (never licensed); at least 1 member 60 or older

flashcards.f: FREC terms and quorum — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: 4-year terms; at most two consecutive terms (plus the rest of a predecessor's term); quorum 4 (51% of 7)

flashcards.f: Duties: no brokerage relationship — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: 3 duties: deal honestly and fairly; disclose known facts materially affecting value of residential property not readily observable; account for all funds

flashcards.f: Duties: transaction broker — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
7 duties: the 3 above + use skill, care and diligence; present all offers and counteroffers timely (unless directed otherwise in writing); limited confidentiality (unless waived in writing); any additional duties mutually agreed
Qualifications: Not a fiduciary.

flashcards.f: Duties: single agent — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
9 duties: honesty/fairness; loyalty; confidentiality; obedience; full disclosure; accounting; skill, care and diligence; presenting offers; disclosing material facts
Conditions: Obedience covers lawful instructions only.
Qualifications: Florida prohibits single agency for both buyer and seller in the same transaction.

flashcards.f: Residential sale (disclosure scope) — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
Improved residential property of 4 units or fewer; unimproved residential property intended for 4 units or fewer; agricultural property of 10 acres or fewer
Qualifications: Not: commercial, leases/rentals (unless an option to buy ≤4 units), auctions, appraisals, business enterprises (except ≤4 residential units), open houses, casual encounters, general factual questions, parties already represented.

flashcards.f: Designated sales associates — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
Nonresidential transaction; buyer and seller each have assets of $1 million or more
Conditions: Requested in writing; disclosures signed.
Qualifications: Never in residential transactions.

flashcards.f: Sales associate delivers deposit to broker — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: No later than the end of the next business day

flashcards.f: Broker deposits escrow funds ('immediately') — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: No later than the end of the third business day after the brokerage receives the funds

flashcards.f: Broker's own money in escrow — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
Up to $1,000 in a sales escrow account; up to $5,000 in a property management escrow account
Qualifications: More than that = commingling.

flashcards.f: Conflicting demands: notice to FREC — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
Within 15 business days after the last demand (or after good-faith doubt arises)
Conditions: Only when the broker holds the funds.
Qualifications: Condo buyer cancels under s. 718.503; buyer's good-faith financing failure.

flashcards.f: Conflicting demands: start a settlement procedure — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: Within 30 business days after the last demand

flashcards.f: Mediation time limit — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: Must be completed within 90 days after the last demand; otherwise promptly use another procedure

flashcards.f: Dispute settles before EDO issues — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: Notify FREC within 10 business days

flashcards.f: Rental information for a fee: refunds — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
Keep at most 25%: refund 75% if no rental is obtained; refund 100% if the information was not current or accurate
Qualifications: Violation: first-degree misdemeanor and license discipline. Older editions: demand within 30 days (not re-confirmed in the current text).

flashcards.f: Record keeping — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: At least 5 years; if the records are involved in litigation, at least 2 years after the case and any appeal end (never less than 5 years in total)

flashcards.f: Administrative fine — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: Up to $5,000 per violation (count)
Up to 10 years

flashcards.f: Unlicensed practice — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: Third-degree felony (up to 5 years in prison and a $5,000 fine under the general sentencing statutes)

flashcards.f: Appeal of a final order — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: Notice of appeal within 30 days after the final order, to the District Court of Appeal

flashcards.f: Recovery Fund caps — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
$50,000 per transaction (all claimants combined); $150,000 aggregate per licensee
Qualifications: No treble damages, court costs, attorney's fees or interest.

flashcards.f: Fair housing protected classes — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: 1866: race (all property, no exceptions). 1968: race, color, religion, national origin. 1974: sex. 1988: familial status and handicap (disability).

flashcards.f: Housing for older persons — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: 55+: at least 80% of occupied units have at least one person 55 or older (with published policies and age verification); or 62+: all occupants 62 or older

flashcards.f: Fair housing exemptions — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
Private owner of no more than 3 single-family homes selling/renting without a broker or discriminatory ads (one sale per 24 months if not the occupant); owner-occupied building of no more than 4 units ('Mrs. Murphy'); religious organizations and private clubs (members, non-commercial)
Conditions: Lost if a broker is used or a discriminatory ad is published.
Qualifications: Never for race (1866 Act).

flashcards.f: Fair housing complaints — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b: HUD complaint within 1 year; lawsuit within 2 years

flashcards.f: Do Not Call established business relationship — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
FCC rule: up to 18 months after a purchase/transaction; up to 3 months after an inquiry. FTC rule (since May 16, 2024): 540 days / 90 days.
Conditions: A specific request not to be called overrides it.
Qualifications: Written permission also allows calls.

flashcards.f: CAN-SPAM opt-out — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
Honored within 10 business days
Qualifications: Every commercial email needs a valid physical postal address.

flashcards.f: TRID timing — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
Loan Estimate within 3 business days after the application; Closing Disclosure received at least 3 business days before consummation (closing)
Qualifications: A corrected Closing Disclosure restarts the 3 days only if the APR becomes inaccurate, the loan product changes, or a prepayment penalty is added.

flashcards.f: TILA right of rescission — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
3 business days
Qualifications: Not for purchase-money loans or investment property.

flashcards.f: Security deposit: notice of how held — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
In the lease or within 30 days of receipt
Qualifications: Not required for landlords who rent fewer than 5 units.

flashcards.f: Security deposit after move-out — state the exact rule.
flashcards.b:
