Registration allowing a sales associate to work for several connected entities of one owner-developer.
Separate licenses a BROKER may hold for separate, unconnected brokerages.
glossary.note: Sales associates cannot hold multiple licenses.

glossary.def: License whose holder is registered with an employing broker (or, for a broker, an office) and may practice.
Status chosen by the licensee; may be renewed indefinitely with CE.
Status caused by failure to renew; expires (void) after 2 years.
The license has ceased to exist; the person must requalify.
A license that exists but cannot be used, e.g., a sales associate with no employing broker.
45-hour course a sales associate must complete before the first renewal.
14 hours every 2-year renewal period after the first: 3 Core Law + 3 Ethics and Business Practices + 8 specialty.
A licensee providing limited representation to a buyer, seller or both; not a fiduciary. Presumed in Florida.
A broker who represents one party (the principal) as a fiduciary.
A licensee works with a party without representing them; owes 3 duties.
Acting as fiduciary agent for both buyer and seller in one transaction; prohibited in Florida.
A person in a relationship of trust who must put the principal's interests first.
The person a single agent represents.
A party a licensee works with but does not represent as a fiduciary.
Transaction-broker duty not to reveal that the seller will accept less, the buyer will pay more, a party's motivation, or other information a party asks to keep confidential.
Signed consent of a principal allowing the single agent to become a transaction broker.
Sale of ≤4 residential units, unimproved land for ≤4 units, or agricultural property ≤10 acres.
A fact that would affect a reasonable person's decision or the property's value.
A hidden defect not discoverable by ordinary inspection.
Associate appointed as single agent for one party in a nonresidential deal where each party has $1M+ in assets.
Account holding money belonging to others (deposits, rents).
Deposit a buyer gives to show good faith, usually held in escrow.
glossary.note: Not the Portuguese 'sinal' — no automatic double-return rule.

glossary.def: Mixing personal or business funds with escrow funds.
Using escrow funds for personal or unauthorized purposes.
Order from FREC deciding who receives disputed escrow funds held by a broker.
Lawsuit in which the broker deposits disputed funds with the court and asks it to decide who is entitled.
Non-binding process with a neutral third party; requires all parties' written consent.
Binding decision by a neutral arbitrator; requires all parties' consent.
Advertisement that fails to include the brokerage's registered name.
Payment for referring business; restricted by Chapter 475 and prohibited by RESPA in most residential financed deals.
Competitors agreeing on commission rates; illegal under antitrust law.
Additional location where the broker conducts business; must be registered.
A complaint alleging facts that, if true, would violate a statute or rule.
Panel that decides whether the investigation supports filing a formal complaint.
Judge from the Division of Administrative Hearings who conducts formal hearings and recommends an order.
FREC's decision on discipline.
Fixed fine for a listed minor violation, offered instead of formal proceedings.
Written notice for a first minor violation, letting the licensee correct it.
Reckless indifference to others' rights — more than simple carelessness.
False statement or concealment of a material fact.
State fund that pays consumers who cannot collect a judgment against a licensee arising from a brokerage transaction.
Directing buyers or renters toward or away from areas based on a protected class.
Inducing owners to sell by suggesting a protected class is moving in.
A lender refusing loans or changing terms in certain areas for discriminatory reasons.
Households with children under 18, pregnant women, or people obtaining custody.
Physical change to a unit for a person with a disability, generally at the tenant's expense.
Change in rules or policies for a person with a disability (e.g., assistance animal despite a no-pets rule).
Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act: closing disclosures and anti-kickback rules for federally related residential loans.
Truth in Lending Act: disclosure of credit costs, APR, advertising trigger terms, right of rescission.
Annual percentage rate: the yearly cost of credit including interest and certain fees.
Specific credit term in an ad (down payment amount, payment amount, number of payments, finance charge) that requires full disclosure.
TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure rule: Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure.

Equal Credit Opportunity Act: no credit discrimination by race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age (if able to contract), public assistance income, or good-faith exercise of consumer credit rights.
Americans with Disabilities Act: accessibility of public accommodations and commercial facilities.
Home Mortgage Disclosure Act: lenders report lending data that reveals patterns like redlining.
Ownership rights: possession, control, enjoyment, exclusion, disposition.
Ownership of indeterminate duration (fee simple, life estate).
The most complete ownership, inheritable and unconditional.
Ownership that can be lost if a stated condition occurs or is breached.
Ownership limited to the life of a person.
glossary.note: Similar in purpose to usufruto, but a distinct legal form.

glossary.def: Life estate measured by the life of someone other than the life tenant.
Future interest passing to a third party when a life estate ends.
Future interest returning to the grantor (or heirs) when a life estate ends.
Damage or neglect by a life tenant that harms the future interest.
Right of possession under a lease, without ownership.
Lease for a fixed term (any length); ends without notice.
Lease renewing period to period (week, month, quarter, year) until notice.
Tenancy of indefinite duration terminable by proper notice.
Holdover tenant who stays without the landlord's consent.
Tenant pays fixed rent; landlord pays operating expenses.
Tenant pays rent plus some or all property expenses (triple net: taxes, insurance, maintenance).
Rent includes a percentage of the tenant's gross sales, usually above a base rent.
Long-term lease of land on which the tenant builds.
Transfer of the ENTIRE remaining lease term.
Transfer of part of the remaining term or part of the space.
Co-ownership with undivided, possibly unequal shares and no survivorship.

glossary.term: Joint tenancy with right of survivorship
glossary.def: Co-ownership with the four unities; deceased owner's share passes to survivors.
Ownership by a married couple as one unit; survivorship; protected from one spouse's creditors.
Possession, Interest, Time, Title.
Court action to divide co-owned property or force its sale.
A Florida owner's primary residence, with creditor protection, transfer restrictions, and tax exemption.
Ownership of a unit in fee simple plus an undivided share of common elements, created by a recorded declaration.
Parts of a condominium owned in common (lobby, pool, roof).
A corporation owns the building; residents own shares and hold proprietary leases (personal property).
Lease giving a co-op shareholder the right to occupy a unit.
Right to use a unit for a set period each year.
Homeowners' association: mandatory-membership community governed by recorded covenants.
Community Development District: special-purpose local government that finances community infrastructure through assessments.
Ownership and the evidence of it.
Property passing to the state when an owner dies without a will or heirs.
Government's power to take private property for public use with just compensation (condemnation).
Acquiring title by open, notorious, hostile, continuous possession for 7 years in Florida plus color of title or payment of taxes.
A document that appears to give title but is defective.
Dying with / without a valid will.
Gift of real property by will / its recipient.
Transfer of an intestate's property to heirs under statute.
The person conveying / receiving title by deed.
Grantor warrants title against defects from any time.
Grantor warrants only against defects arising during their ownership.
Implies the grantor owns the property but gives no warranties.
Conveys whatever interest the grantor has, with no warranties.
A claim or defect that impairs title.
Formal declaration before a notary that the signer signed voluntarily; needed to record.
Covenant that the grantor owns the property and has the right to convey it.
Notice the law presumes from public records or visible possession.
What a person actually knows.
Summary of all recorded documents affecting a property's title.
Policy protecting against losses from title defects existing before the policy date.
Any claim or limitation on title (lien, easement, restriction, encroachment).
A claim against property as security for a debt.
Lien on one property (mortgage, property tax, construction lien).
Lien on all the debtor's property (judgment, IRS lien).
A lienholder agreeing to a lower priority.
Easement benefiting an adjoining parcel (dominant) over a burdened parcel (servient); runs with the land.
Easement benefiting a person or company (e.g., utility), not a parcel.
Easement acquired by 20 years of open, continuous, adverse use in Florida.
Revocable personal permission to use land; not an interest in land.
glossary.note: Different meaning from a real estate license.

glossary.def: A structure or improvement extending onto another's land.
Private limitation on use recorded in a deed or plat.
Personal property attached to real property so that it becomes part of it.
Item a business tenant installs for its trade; remains the tenant's personal property.
Annual crops produced by labor; personal property.
Rights of owners along rivers and streams.
Rights of owners along oceans, seas and large lakes.
Gradual addition of land by water deposits (owner gains) / sudden loss or change (boundary does not move).
Description using a point of beginning, directions (courses) and distances, returning to the POB.
Starting and ending point of a metes-and-bounds description.
Description by lot and block numbers on a recorded plat.
Recorded map of a subdivision.
System of townships and sections measured from principal meridians and base lines.
6 × 6 mile square, 36 sections.
1 square mile, 640 acres.
A foot of frontage along a street or water; the first dimension given.
Promise for a promise (e.g., sale contract).
Promise for an act (e.g., option, reward).
Obligations still to perform / fully performed.
No contract at all / one party may cancel / valid but courts won't enforce.
Law requiring certain contracts (sale of real estate, >1 year) to be written and signed.
Something of value exchanged; mutual promises suffice.
A response that changes the terms; it rejects and terminates the original offer.
Contract giving the optionee the right to buy at set terms during a period; optionor is bound.
Buyer's interest under a signed sale contract before closing.
Court order to perform the contract as agreed.
Damages agreed in advance (often the deposit).
The broker whose efforts started an uninterrupted chain of events leading to the sale.
Listing given to several brokers; only the procuring broker is paid; owner may sell free.
One brokerage; owner keeps the right to sell without commission.
One brokerage earns the commission no matter who sells.
Broker keeps any amount above the seller's net price.
Date the last party signs or initials the final offer/counteroffer and it is communicated; contract deadlines run from it.
Clause making contract deadlines strict.
Seller makes no repairs; buyer may inspect and cancel within the inspection period.
The borrower's written promise to repay the debt.
Security instrument pledging property for a debt.
glossary.note: In US usage 'mortgage' is the document, not the loan.

glossary.def: Borrower (gives the mortgage) / lender (receives it).
The borrower keeps title; the lender holds a lien (Florida).
Lets the lender demand the entire balance on default.
Balance becomes due if the property is transferred.
The mortgage is defeated (cancelled) when the debt is paid.
Borrower not personally liable; lender looks only to the property.
Buyer takes over the loan and becomes personally liable.
Substitution of a new party that releases the original borrower.
Buyer takes title and pays the loan without personal liability.
Borrower's right to pay off the debt and stop foreclosure until the sale.
Judgment for the unpaid balance after a foreclosure sale.
Sale where the lender accepts less than the amount owed.
Borrower deeds the property to the lender to avoid foreclosure; junior liens survive.
Principal, interest, taxes, insurance — the monthly housing payment.
Charging interest above the legal maximum.
Loan-to-value ratio: loan ÷ lesser of price or appraised value.
Federal Housing Administration (HUD): insures loans; borrower pays MIP.
Department of Veterans Affairs: guarantees loans to eligible veterans.
Private mortgage insurance on conventional loans above 80% LTV.
Level payments covering interest and principal until fully repaid.
Large final payment on a partially amortized loan.
Adjustable-rate mortgage: rate = index + margin, limited by caps.
Covers real and personal property.
Covers several parcels; release clause frees parcels as paid.
New junior loan that includes an existing loan.
Seller finances part of the price.
Lender pays an owner aged 62+; repaid on sale, move-out or death.
Lenders who originate loans.
Buyers of existing loans (Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, Ginnie Mae guarantees).
Depositors withdrawing funds for higher yields elsewhere, reducing mortgage money.
Prepaid interest: 1 point = 1% of the loan.
Dividing an expense or income between buyer and seller as of closing.
Paid at the end of the period (Florida property taxes, mortgage interest).
Paid at the start of the period (rent, insurance premiums).
An amount a party owes at closing.
An amount a party receives at closing.
Florida excise tax on deeds ($0.70/$100) and notes ($0.35/$100).
Florida one-time tax of 2 mills on new mortgages.
Comparative market analysis by a licensee to suggest a price range.
Broker price opinion, often for lenders; chargeable but not an appraisal.
Most probable price in an arm's-length sale between informed parties under no unusual pressure.
Legally permissible, physically possible, financially feasible, maximally productive use.
A buyer won't pay more than the cost of an equally desirable substitute.
Value increase from combining parcels / the act of combining them.
Weighing the approaches to reach a final value estimate (not averaging).
Cost of an exact replica.
Cost of a building with equal utility using current materials.
Loss from outdated design or features.
Loss from factors outside the property; always incurable.
Net operating income: effective gross income minus operating expenses.
NOI ÷ value.
Gross rent multiplier (price ÷ monthly rent) / gross income multiplier (price ÷ annual income).
Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice.
Using borrowed money to increase return on equity.
NOI minus debt service.
Selling a business (goodwill, inventory, fixtures, possibly real estate).
Intangible value of a business's reputation and customer base.
According to value.
Florida's term for market value used by the property appraiser.
Truth in Millage notice showing proposed assessments and rates (August).
County board that hears property assessment appeals.
Lien sold to an investor to collect delinquent property taxes.
Charge on properties specially benefited by a public improvement.
Tax rate in mills (1 mill = $1 per $1,000 of taxable value).
Cap on annual homestead assessment increases (3% or CPI, whichever is less).
Cost of property / cost plus improvements minus depreciation.
Tax-deferred exchange of like-kind investment or business real property.
Non-like-kind value received in an exchange; taxable to the extent of gain.
Seller receives payments over time and reports gain as received.
Government power to regulate for health, safety and welfare; no compensation owed.
Owner's lawsuit claiming a regulation amounts to a taking.
Local government's long-range land-use plan; zoning implements it.
Permission to deviate from a dimensional rule because of hardship unique to the parcel.
Use allowed in a zone with case-by-case approval.
Lawful use that predates current zoning ('grandfathered').
Planned unit development mixing uses with clustered density and open space.
Document allowing a building to be occupied after final inspection.
Federal law imposing strict, joint and several liability for cleaning up contaminated sites.
Abandoned or underused contaminated site being redeveloped.
Naturally occurring radioactive gas; Florida requires a disclosure in sale and lease contracts.

verification.manual: 100 questions, 3.5 hours, 75 to pass.
verification.finding: Candidate Information Booklet (Sales Associate, effective January 2025): 100 multiple-choice questions, 3.5 hours, 75 or higher passes, 19 content areas.
verification.citation: DBPR Candidate Information Booklet, Real Estate Sales Associate Examination (Jan 2025)
verification.teach: 100 questions · 3.5 hours · 75 correct to pass.

verification.manual: About 45 law, 45 principles and practices, 10 math.
verification.finding: Candidate Information Booklet, Sales Associate (eff. January 2025), Examination Content Outline: I The Real Estate Business 1%; II License Law and Qualifications for Licensure 6%; III License Law and Commission Rules 2%; IV Authorized Relationships, Duties and Disclosure 7%; V Brokerage Activities and Procedures 12%; VI Violations of License Law, Penalties and Procedures 3%; VII Federal and State Laws 3%; VIII Property Rights 8%; IX Title, Deeds and Ownership Restrictions 7%; X Legal Descriptions 5%; XI Contracts 12%; XII Residential Mortgages 9%; XIII Types of Mortgages and Sources of Financing 4%; XIV Computations and Closing 6%; XV Markets and Analysis 1%; XVI Appraisal 8%; XVII Investments and Business Opportunity Brokerage 2%; XVIII Taxes 3%; XIX Planning and Zoning 1% (total 100%). 18 of the 19 figures appeared in official-domain excerpts of the booklet; Section I (1%) is derived from the 100% total. The Broker booklet uses different weights. A 2020 FREC rule document describes a 45/45/10 split (law / principles and practices / math).
verification.citation: DBPR Candidate Information Booklet, Real Estate Sales Associate Examination (eff. Jan 2025), Examination Content Outline
verification.teach: Weights per FREC section as listed. The biggest: Brokerage Activities 12%, Contracts 12%, Residential Mortgages 9%, Property Rights 8%, Appraisal 8%. The app's mock exam follows these weights.

verification.manual: Manual compresses the 19 Gold Coast chapters into 12.
verification.finding: FREC Sales Associate Course Syllabus (FREC Course I), effective 1/1/2023, has 19 sections: 1 Course Overview: The Real Estate Business; 2 Real Estate License Law and Qualifications for Licensure; 3 Real Estate License Law and Commission Rules; 4 Authorized Relationships, Duties and Disclosure; 5 Real Estate Brokerage Activities and Procedures; 6 Violations of License Law, Penalties and Procedures; 7 Federal and State Laws Pertaining to Real Estate; 8 Property Rights: Estates, Tenancies, Condominiums, Cooperatives, HOAs and Time-Sharing; 9 Title, Deeds and Ownership Restrictions; 10 Legal Descriptions; 11 Real Estate Contracts; 12 Residential Mortgages; 13 Types of Mortgages and Sources of Financing; 14 Real Estate Related Computations and Closing of Transactions; 15 The Real Estate Markets and Analysis; 16 Real Estate Appraisal; 17 Real Estate Investments and Business Opportunity Brokerage; 18 Taxes Affecting Real Estate; 19 Planning and Zoning. Rule 61J2-3.008: 63 hours of 50 minutes each, inclusive of the course exam.
verification.citation: FREC Course I syllabus (eff. 1/1/2023); Rule 61J2-3.008, F.A.C.
verification.teach: The curriculum uses these 19 sections as its chapter structure.

verification.topic: Termination notice for tenancies without a specific term (s. 83.57)
verification.manual: Week 7 days, month 15 days, quarter 45 days, year 60 days.
verification.finding: Current s. 83.57 (2025 text): year-to-year not less than 60 days; quarter-to-quarter not less than 30 days; month-to-month not less than 30 days; week-to-week not less than 7 days. The 2014 text had 15 days for month-to-month. No version found with 45 days for quarter-to-quarter.
verification.teach: 60 / 30 / 30 / 7 days. If a practice question uses 15 days for month-to-month it reflects the pre-change law; answer with current law unless the question says otherwise, and note the edition of the question source.

verification.manual: Florida requires two witnesses for leases over one year.
verification.finding: Current s. 689.01 still requires two subscribing witnesses for conveyances of freehold estates and terms over one year, but now provides that no subscribing witnesses are required for a lease of real property. The proviso is in the 2024 text and absent in 2010-2019 texts. Witnesses may sign electronically through audio-video technology (s. 117.201).
verification.teach: Deeds: two witnesses. Leases: no witnesses required (a lease over one year must still be in writing under the statute of frauds).

verification.manual: Lists 'flood-zone awareness (via forms)'.
verification.finding: s. 689.302 (created by CS/CS/HB 1049, 2024) requires the seller of residential real property to give the buyer a flood disclosure, on a prescribed form, at or before the time the sales contract is executed. The form covers flood insurance (homeowners' policies do not cover flood), past flood insurance claims, federal flood assistance received, and known flood damage.
verification.teach: Residential seller gives a statutory flood disclosure at or before contract. Effective date not confirmed in this session.

verification.manual: Not mentioned.
verification.finding: s. 83.512, F.S., created by ch. 2025-166, Laws of Fla. (CS/CS/SB 948, effective October 1, 2025), requires a landlord to give a prospective tenant a flood disclosure, as a separate document on the statutory form, at or before signing a residential rental agreement for a term of 1 year or longer. The form covers flood damage the landlord knows of during the landlord's ownership, flood insurance claims (including NFIP) and federal assistance (e.g., FEMA) received for flood damage, plus flood insurance notices. Remedy: if the landlord fails to comply and the tenant suffers a substantial loss of personal property from flooding (repair or replacement cost of 50% or more of its market value), the tenant may terminate the lease by written notice and surrender of possession within 30 days after the damage; prepaid rent for the period after termination is refunded. HB 1015 (2025) was laid on the table; its companion SB 948 was enacted and also amended the seller disclosure in s. 689.302.
verification.citation: s. 83.512, F.S. (2025; same core text 2026); ch. 2025-166, Laws of Fla. (CS/CS/SB 948)
verification.teach: Residential lease of 1 year or longer: landlord gives the flood disclosure at or before signing (since Oct 1, 2025). Shorter leases are not covered. Older books will not mention it.

verification.manual: 3 business days after receiving the documents on a resale.
verification.finding: Nondeveloper (resale) contracts for residential condominium units must say, in conspicuous type, either that the buyer received the declaration, articles, bylaws, rules and other documents more than 7 days (excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays) before signing, or that the agreement is voidable by the buyer by written notice within 7 days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, after the buyer signs and receives the documents. A non-conforming contract is voidable by the buyer before closing; the right ends at closing. CS/CS/HB 913 (ch. 2025-175, effective July 1, 2025) extended this period from 3 days to 7 days; the 2024 text still read 3 days. Developer sales (unchanged): voidable within 15 days after the buyer signs and receives all required documents, and within 15 days after receiving an amendment that materially and adversely changes the offering; waivers are void; the right ends at closing.
verification.citation: s. 718.503(1)(a), (2), F.S. (2025; 7-day text also in 2026); ch. 2025-175, Laws of Fla. (CS/CS/HB 913); Senate 2025 Summary of Legislation Passed
verification.teach: Developer sale: 15 days. Resale: 7 days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays, after signing and receiving the documents (since July 1, 2025; older books say 3 business days). Both rights end at closing.

verification.topic: Second homestead exemption indexed to inflation (s. 196.031)
verification.manual: Additional $25,000 on assessed value between $50,000 and $75,000, non-school.
verification.finding: Amendment 5 (approved Nov 5, 2024, effective Jan 1, 2025) indexes the additional exemption to CPI-U when the change is positive. Florida DOR: $25,722 for 2025 (2.9% CPI). Still applies only to non-school levies on assessed value over $50,000.
verification.citation: s. 196.031(1)(b), F.S.; Fla. DOR 2025 CPI adjustment notice
verification.teach: First $25,000: all taxes. Second exemption: up to $25,000 (CPI-indexed since 2025) on value above $50,000, non-school only. Exam math usually uses the round $25,000.

verification.topic: Widow/widower, blind, totally and permanently disabled exemption (s. 196.202)
verification.manual: $5,000 (raised from $500 by 2023 law).
verification.finding: Current statute: $5,000. Increase enacted by the 2022 Legislature, first applying to the 2023 tax roll.
verification.citation: s. 196.202, F.S.; Fla. DOR PTO Bulletin 22-05
verification.teach: $5,000. Older printings say $500.

verification.topic: Reactivating an involuntarily inactive license (s. 475.183; Rule 61J2-3.010)
verification.manual: Reactivate within 2 years by completing late CE.
verification.finding: Involuntarily inactive 12 months or less: complete at least 14 hours of commission-prescribed CE. More than 12 but fewer than 24 months: complete 28 hours of a commission-prescribed reactivation course. Involuntarily inactive more than 2 years: license expires (null and void).
verification.teach: ≤12 months → 14 hours. 12–24 months → 28-hour course. >24 months → void.

verification.manual: Unlicensed practice is a third-degree felony; most other criminal violations are misdemeanors.
verification.finding: s. 475.42(1)(a): operating as a broker or sales associate without a valid, current, active license is a third-degree felony. s. 475.42(2): any other violation of subsection (1) is a second-degree misdemeanor (s. 775.082 or 775.083), unless the chapter prescribes a different punishment.
verification.teach: Unlicensed activity = third-degree felony (up to 5 years and $5,000 under the general sentencing statutes). Other s. 475.42(1) violations = second-degree misdemeanor.

verification.manual: 7 members, Governor appoints, Senate confirms, 4 brokers (5 yrs), 1 broker or sales associate (2 yrs), 2 consumers, one member 60+, 4-year terms, quorum 4, two-term limit.
verification.finding: Confirmed: 7 members appointed by the Governor subject to Senate confirmation; 4 licensed brokers with active licenses for the 5 preceding years; 1 broker or sales associate with an active license for the 2 preceding years; 2 members who are not and have never been brokers or sales associates; at least one member 60 or older; 4-year terms (s. 475.02). Quorum: 51% or more of the appointed members (s. 455.207) = 4 of 7; official action needs a majority of the quorum. Term limit (s. 20.165(5)): no member serves more than the remainder of a predecessor's term plus two consecutive 4-year terms; terms end October 31.
verification.teach: 7 members (4 brokers, 1 broker or sales associate, 2 consumers; one 60+); 4-year terms; quorum 4; at most two consecutive full terms.

verification.manual: Includes 'radon/appraiser/CPA professionals' and 'attorneys-in-fact under a power of attorney for a single specific transaction'.
verification.finding: Statute exempts, among others: attorneys in fact acting for the execution of contracts or conveyances only; attorneys at law within their duties; CPAs within their duties; personal representatives, receivers, trustees, and others appointed by will or court order; salaried employees of public utilities, railroads, government agencies acting for the employer's property; owners selling or leasing their own property (unless they use commissioned agents in the ordinary course of business); salaried employees of an owner (or of a broker for an owner) of an apartment community working in an onsite rental office in a leasing capacity; salaried condominium/cooperative managers renting units for terms of 1 year or less. No radon exemption found.
verification.teach: Teach the statutory list. Drop 'radon'.

verification.manual: Notify FREC within 15 business days; institute a procedure within 30 business days; mediation 90 days; notify within 10 business days if parties settle.
verification.finding: Rule 61J2-10.032 (eff. 5/21/2024): written notice to the Commission within 15 business days of the last demand (or of having good-faith doubt); institute a settlement procedure within 30 business days. Procedures: escrow disbursement order, arbitration (all parties consent), interpleader/litigation, mediation (all parties consent in writing; must be completed within 90 days after the last demand, otherwise promptly use another procedure). If the matter settles or goes to court before an EDO issues, notify the Commission within 10 business days. Following the resulting order protects the licensee from discipline for failure to account.
verification.teach: 15 / 30 business days; mediation 90 days; 10 business days if settled.

verification.topic: When a broker may return a deposit without notifying FREC (s. 475.25(1)(d)1)
verification.manual: Exceptions: title company or attorney holds the deposit; HUD sale; condominium buyer rescission.
verification.finding: Statute: if a residential condominium buyer delivers written notice of intent to cancel under s. 718.503, or if a buyer in good faith fails to satisfy the terms of the financing clause, the licensee may return the escrowed property to the purchaser without notifying the commission or starting a settlement procedure. No HUD exception found in the excerpts.
verification.teach: Statutory exceptions: condo buyer cancels under 718.503; buyer's good-faith financing failure. When a title company or attorney holds the deposit, the broker is not the escrow holder and follows the verification procedure in V-39. 'HUD' removed (no official source found).

verification.manual: $50,000 per transaction, $150,000 per licensee; no punitive damages or interest; license suspended until repaid with interest.
verification.finding: Payment is the lesser of the unsatisfied judgment (actual or compensatory damages) or $50,000; treble damages, court costs, attorney's fees and interest are not recoverable; $50,000 aggregate per transaction regardless of claimants; $150,000 aggregate per licensee (prorated when exceeded). Automatic suspension on payment until repaid in full plus interest (seen in 2010 text; not visible in the 2026 excerpt).
verification.teach: $50,000 per transaction · $150,000 per licensee · actual/compensatory damages only.

verification.manual: Deed $0.70 per $100 (Miami-Dade $0.60 single-family, other property $0.60 + $0.45 surtax); note $0.35 per $100; round up to next $100.
verification.finding: Deeds: 70 cents on each $100 or portion thereof of the total consideration in all counties except Miami-Dade, where the rate is 60 cents per $100. Miami-Dade also levies a discretionary surtax of 45 cents per $100 (s. 201.031; s. 125.0167 limits it to Miami-Dade) on documents other than those involving only a single-family residence, for a combined $1.05 per $100. Existing mortgage balance counts as consideration. Notes/written obligations: 35 cents per $100 or portion; capped at $2,450 only for unsecured documents; no cap for mortgage-secured obligations.
verification.citation: ss. 201.02, 201.031, 201.08, F.S. (2026); Fla. DOR documentary stamp tax page and Form DR-228 instructions
verification.teach: Deed $0.70/$100 or portion (round UP), on the full price. Note $0.35/$100 or portion. Miami-Dade: $0.60 for a single-family residence; other property $0.60 + $0.45 surtax.

verification.manual: 2 mills on new mortgages only, no rounding.
verification.finding: One-time tax of 2 mills on the just valuation of obligations secured by a mortgage or lien on Florida real property; paid when the mortgage is recorded.
verification.teach: 0.002 × new mortgage amount.

verification.manual: Apply to residential sales (≤4 units, unimproved for ≤4 units, agricultural ≤10 acres); not to commercial, leases, auctions, appraisals, business brokerage.
verification.finding: Definition confirmed. Disclosure not required: when the licensee knows the party is already represented by a single agent or transaction broker; bona fide open houses or model showings with no confidential information, offer, or representation agreement; unanticipated casual encounters; responses to general factual questions about advertised property; communications limited to general information about the licensee's qualifications or firm; auctions; appraisals; rentals and leases unless they include an option to purchase property with four or fewer residential units; dispositions of business enterprises except property with four or fewer residential units. Also a developer's onsite employees selling new units (manual-independent; not seen in excerpt).
verification.teach: Full exception list.

verification.manual: 75% refund if no rental obtained, demand within 30 days; full refund if list inaccurate; first-degree misdemeanor.
verification.finding: s. 475.453(1) (2025): a broker or sales associate who furnishes a rental information list for a fee paid by the prospective tenant must give a contract or receipt providing for repayment of any amount over 25% of the fee if no rental is obtained, and repayment of the full fee on demand if the information was not current or accurate in any material respect. s. 475.453(3)(a): violation is a first-degree misdemeanor; (3)(b): the license is also subject to suspension or revocation. The 30-day window for demanding the refund appears in the 2002/2005 editions; the 2025 excerpts did not show it.
verification.teach: 75% refund if no rental is obtained; full refund if the list was inaccurate; violation = first-degree misdemeanor plus license discipline. The 30-day demand window is from older editions (not re-confirmed).

verification.manual: Agreements with several states; nonresidents only; 40-question Florida law exam, 30 correct.
verification.finding: DBPR's mutual recognition page and the Real Estate Laws and Rules candidate booklet: applicants from a state with a current agreement pass a 40-question Florida law exam, 30 or more correct. The applicant must not be a Florida resident when applying, and the other state's license must have been earned by education and exam there (not by reciprocity). Statutory basis s. 475.180. The Division home page lists 9 states (Alabama, Arkansas, Connecticut, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi, Nebraska, Rhode Island, West Virginia) and lists Illinois as 'Agreement Dissolved – December 31, 2025', along with Colorado (2009), Tennessee (2012), Indiana (2014) and Oklahoma (2016). A March 2025 FREC agenda item amended the West Virginia agreement. The Licensure Information page still listing Illinois appears out of date. Evidence: search excerpts only; the Illinois dissolution date appears on one page.
verification.citation: DBPR Division of Real Estate home page and mutual recognition page (2026 excerpts); RE_law_cibs.pdf; s. 475.180, F.S.
verification.teach: Mechanism and the 40/30 exam: know them. Current list (9): AL, AR, CT, GA, KY, MS, NE, RI, WV; Illinois ended December 31, 2025. The list changes; low exam priority.

verification.topic: Proposed homestead property-tax amendment (CS/HJR 1-F, 2026 Special Session)
verification.manual: Not mentioned.
verification.finding: Passed both chambers June 2, 2026; filed with the Secretary of State June 16, 2026; goes to the November 2026 ballot. Summaries describe a larger homestead exemption for non-school taxes and a lower cap on non-homestead assessment increases. Not law unless approved by voters.
verification.citation: CS/HJR 1-F (2026F)
verification.teach: Not exam content. Watch the November 2026 result; exam questions usually lag law changes.

verification.manual: Table shows an assumed mortgage as a buyer credit only.
verification.finding: An assumed mortgage is a double entry: credit the buyer (it pays part of the price) and debit the seller (the seller hands over the debt instead of paying it off from proceeds). A new mortgage is a buyer credit only; the seller's payoff of an existing loan is a seller debit only.
verification.citation: Closing-statement accounting logic (standard textbook treatment); verify against Gold Coast Ch. 14
verification.teach: Assumed mortgage: debit seller, credit buyer.

verification.manual: Note stamps apply to new and assumed mortgages; intangible tax only to new money.
verification.finding: Florida DOR lists 'mortgages and assumptions of mortgages' among obligations taxable when recorded, at 35 cents per $100 or portion (s. 201.08; no cap for recorded mortgages). DOR TAA 22B4-002: assuming a note and mortgage is a taxable renewal under s. 201.08(1), measured on the outstanding balance. Intangible tax: s. 199.145(3) — no additional nonrecurring tax is due when an obligation is assumed if the tax was paid before and the debt is unchanged; refinancing with the same lender is taxed only on new principal (s. 199.145(4)).
verification.citation: s. 201.08(1), F.S.; ss. 199.133, 199.145(3)-(4), F.S. (2025); Fla. DOR documentary stamp tax page; DOR TAA 22B4-002
verification.teach: Note stamps ($0.35/$100) on new AND assumed mortgages. Intangible tax (2 mills) on new mortgages only — not again on an assumption when it was paid originally and the debt is unchanged.

verification.manual: Minimum age, education and SSN for applicants; reapplying 2 years after a denial for dishonesty; the 3/7/9 brokerage duty lists (s. 475.278); statute of frauds; qualifying ratios 28/36 and 31/43; PMI above 80% LTV; FHA 3.5% down; points ≈ 1/8% yield; reverse mortgage age 62; Florida meridian intersection in Tallahassee; measurement constants (acre, mile, square yard, township, section).
verification.finding: The 2026-10-19/20 verification passes checked the other manual statements (V-27 to V-80). These remain from the study manual. Measurement constants are standard definitions; ratios, PMI, points and FHA figures are course conventions or program rules that change over time.
verification.citation: Study manual
verification.teach: Taught as stated, labelled 'not yet verified'. Next verification pass: s. 475.278 duty lists and s. 475.17(1) applicant requirements.

verification.manual: Sales associates must complete 45 hours of post-licensing education before the first renewal; otherwise the license becomes null and void and the person must requalify [s. 475.17(3), F.S.; Rule 61J2-3.020, F.A.C.]
verification.finding: s. 475.17(3)(a) lets the Commission prescribe postlicensure education for a sales associate to keep a valid license. The cap is 45 classroom hours of 50 minutes each, including the exam, and it is due before the first renewal after initial licensure. It is delivered as one or more Commission-approved courses totaling at least 45 hours, by classroom or approved distance learning (distance courses need a passed timed exam). A completion notice is withheld if absences exceed 10% of classroom hours. If the requirement is not done before the first renewal, the license 'shall be considered null and void.' To operate again the person must requalify by completing the sales associate prelicensure course and passing the state exam. Exceptions: the Commission may allow an extra 6 months for an individual physical hardship defined by rule, and holders of a 4-year or higher degree in real estate are exempt. Attorneys are NOT exempt from post-licensing, per DBPR. DBPR's current 2026 renewal notices still list 45 hours for sales associates. Rule 61J2-3.020 says the same, but the only rule text seen was a 2017 FREC meeting copy, so the current rule text was not read directly.
verification.citation: s. 475.17(3)(a),(c), F.S. (2025 and 2026 editions); Rule 61J2-3.020, F.A.C.; DBPR Division of Real Estate 2026 renewal notice (SL AC Grp 1)
verification.teach: 45 hours before the first renewal. Missed → license null and void → retake the 63-hour course and pass the state exam again. Exempt: holders of a 4-year (or higher) degree in real estate. Attorneys are NOT exempt. FREC may allow 6 more months for a physical hardship.

verification.manual: After the first renewal, 14 hours of continuing education (including core law) each 2-year renewal period, for active and inactive licensees [s. 475.182, F.S.; Rule 61J2-3.009]
verification.finding: s. 475.182(1): the renewal application for an active broker, broker associate or sales associate license must include proof of at least 14 classroom hours (50-minute hours) of continuing education in each biennium of the license period. Approved distance learning is allowed. Sales associates and brokers do not have to meet the 14-hour requirement before the first renewal after initial licensure, because postlicensure education applies then. Rule 61J2-3.009 is titled 'Continuing Education for Active and Inactive Broker and Sales Associate Licensees.' It requires every active or inactive licensee to complete at least 14 hours (50-minute hours) per renewal period, excluding the first renewal period. As amended, the 14 hours are 3 hours Core Law, 3 hours Ethics and Business Practices, and 8 hours specialty education. This split is mandatory for licenses expiring on or after March 31, 2025. Core Law must be taken at least once per renewal period. Other points: Florida Bar members in good standing are exempt from CE under this rule. Once per renewal cycle, attending one FREC legal agenda session may substitute for 3 hours, with 7 days' notice, but not when attending as a party to a disciplinary action. Note that the manual's 'including core law' is now more specific: 3 Core Law + 3 Ethics + 8 specialty.
verification.citation: s. 475.182(1), F.S. (2025/2026 editions); Rule 61J2-3.009, F.A.C. (current); FREC education page; DBPR 2025/2026 renewal notices
verification.teach: 14 hours in each 2-year renewal period after the first renewal, for active and inactive licensees: 3 hours Core Law + 3 hours Ethics and Business Practices + 8 hours specialty. Florida Bar members are exempt from CE. Once per cycle, attending a FREC legal agenda session can replace 3 hours.

verification.topic: Broker licence: experience and pre-licence course (s. 475.17(1)-(2))
verification.manual: Broker applicant must have held an active sales associate license for 24 months during the preceding 5 years and complete a 72-hour broker course [s. 475.17(2), F.S.; Rule 61J2-3.008]
verification.finding: Experience: a person may not be licensed as a broker unless one of three things holds during the preceding 5 years, each for at least 24 months. (1) They held an active sales associate license in the office of one or more brokers licensed in Florida, another US state, territory or jurisdiction, or a foreign national jurisdiction. (2) They held a current, valid sales associate license while employed by a governmental agency for a salary, performing licensee duties. (3) They held a current, valid broker license in another US state, territory or jurisdiction, or a foreign jurisdiction. Anyone licensed as a Florida sales associate in the preceding 5 years must also have completed the sales associate postlicensure education. Course: the broker prelicensure course may not exceed 72 classroom hours (50-minute hours) including the exam (FREC Course II), versus 63 hours for sales associates. A completion notice is withheld if absences exceed 8 classroom hours. Citation note: the 72-hour course is in s. 475.17(2)(a)1. The 24-month experience rule is in subsection (1) of s. 475.17, which excerpts label (1)(b), with the postlicensure prerequisite at (1)(c); it is not in (2). The 2026 text matches 2025.
verification.teach: 24 months of experience in the preceding 5 years: as an active sales associate under a broker (Florida, another state or a foreign jurisdiction), as a salaried government employee holding a sales associate licence, or as a broker licensed elsewhere. Sales associate post-licensing must be complete. Then the 72-hour broker course (FREC Course II) and the broker exam.

verification.manual: Brokers must complete 60 hours of post-licensing education before the first broker renewal (two 30-hour courses); otherwise the broker license is void [s. 475.17(3), F.S.; Rule 61J2-3.020]
verification.finding: s. 475.17(4)(a): the Commission may prescribe postlicensure education for a broker to keep a valid license. The cap is 60 classroom hours of 50 minutes each, including the exam, due before the first renewal after initial licensure, as Commission-approved courses totaling at least 60 hours. s. 475.17(4)(c): the license of any broker who does not complete it before the first renewal 'shall be considered null and void.' DBPR guidance: the 60 hours may be taken as two 30-hour courses, Broker Investment and Broker Management, by classroom or distance education. The only exemption is a 4-year degree in real estate; attorneys are not exempt. Re-entry, from the statute and law book (not confirmed in the current subsection text): a former broker whose license became void may get a sales associate license by completing the 14-hour CE course within 6 months after the broker license expired. To be a broker again, they must retake the broker prelicensure course and pass the broker exam. Citation note: the broker provision is s. 475.17(4); (3) is the sales associate provision.
verification.citation: s. 475.17(4)(a),(c), F.S. (2025/2026 editions); Rule 61J2-3.020, F.A.C.; DBPR Division of Real Estate home page and broker guidance
verification.teach: 60 hours before the first broker renewal (usually two 30-hour courses). Missed → broker licence null and void.

verification.topic: Validity of the pre-licence course completion (s. 475.181(2))
verification.manual: Completion of the 63-hour sales associate pre-license course is valid for 2 years for purposes of taking the state exam [s. 475.17, F.S.; Rule 61J2-3.008]
verification.finding: s. 475.181(2): if an applicant does not pass the licensing exam within 2 years after the successful course completion date, the course completion is invalid for licensure. DBPR's sales associate requirements sheet says the 63-hour prelicensing course is valid for licensure for 2 years after completion; the broker sheet says the same of the 72-hour course. The candidate booklet says an expired course completion is not accepted at the test site, and the course completion certificate must be shown at every exam attempt. Florida Bar members in good standing are exempt from the sales associate prelicense course. Citation correction: the 2-year rule is in s. 475.181(2), F.S., not s. 475.17 or Rule 61J2-3.008. Note also that the rule turns on PASSING the exam within 2 years, not merely taking it.
verification.citation: s. 475.181(2), F.S. (2026 edition; same in 2015-2025); DBPR 'Real Estate Associate Requirements for licensure' (RESLRequirements.pdf); DBPR Sales Associate Candidate Information Booklet
verification.teach: The course completion is invalid if the state exam is not PASSED within 2 years after completing the course.

verification.manual: An application for licensure remains valid for 2 years [Rule 61J2-2 / 61J2-3, F.A.C.]
verification.finding: s. 475.181(2): 'The application shall expire 2 years after the date received if the applicant does not pass the appropriate examination.' The window was 1 year in the 2002 statute and has been 2 years since at least the 2005/2009 editions; the 2026 text keeps it. Clarifications: the 2 years run from the date DBPR receives the application, and the rule is that the application expires if the exam is not passed in that time. It is separate from the 2-year course-completion validity in the same subsection. Citation correction: the source is the statute, s. 475.181(2), F.S., not Rule 61J2-2 or 61J2-3.
verification.teach: The application expires 2 years after DBPR receives it if the applicant has not passed the exam.

verification.topic: Length of the first renewal period
verification.manual: The first renewal falls 18-24 months after initial licensure [Rule 61J2-1.008 or 61J2-3.020, F.A.C.]
verification.finding: The DBPR Division of Real Estate educational requirements sheet (rev. 06/2018) says the first renewal period is 18-24 months and the 2nd and later renewal periods are 24 months. Postlicensure education must be finished before that first renewal: 45 hours for sales associates, 60 for brokers. DBPR renewal pages say all real estate licenses expire at midnight Eastern on March 31 or September 30; that is why the first period varies from 18 to 24 months. Caveats: no official source was found stating the 18-24 month rule in Rule 61J2-1.008 or 61J2-3.020, so the manual's rule citation is unverified. The confirming document is an official 2018 DBPR sheet; nothing current contradicts it, but no current-year restatement was found.
verification.citation: DBPR Division of Real Estate, 'Real Estate (FREC) Educational Requirements' (rev. 06/2018); DBPR renewal notices 2025/2026
verification.teach: First renewal falls 18–24 months after licensure, because all real estate licences expire on March 31 or September 30; later periods are 24 months. (Source: DBPR education sheet; the rule number was not located.)

verification.topic: Change of mailing or e-mail address (Rule 61J2-10.038; s. 455.275)
verification.manual: Licensees must notify DBPR/FREC of a change of mailing address within 10 days [Rule 61J2-10.038, F.A.C.; s. 475.23 or s. 455.275, F.S.]
verification.finding: Statute: s. 455.275(1) makes each DBPR licensee solely responsible for notifying the department in writing of their current mailing address, e-mail address and place of practice. Failing to report a change is a violation and can lead to discipline. Rule: Rule 61J2-10.038, 'Mailing Address: Place of Practice: Requirement for Notification', implements s. 455.275(1) and s. 475.05. The 2020 FREC-approved text requires each licensee and permit holder to notify the Department in writing of the current mailing and e-mail address, and any change to either, within 10 days after the change. A first violation gets a citation; repeat violations lead to disciplinary proceedings. The rule was amended again effective 7/18/2024. Per the DBPR annual report, that amendment changed the definition of 'current mailing address' (striking 'residential' so the brokerage office's physical location can serve). The 2024 text itself was not read, so whether the 10-day period survived is inferred, not directly seen. Related: s. 475.23 separately requires notice within 10 days of a change of business address or employing broker, on a Commission form. A resident licensee who becomes a nonresident must notify the Commission within 60 days.
verification.teach: Notify DBPR in writing within 10 days of a change of mailing or e-mail address. Change of employing broker or business address: within 10 days (s. 475.23). The 10-day period is confirmed in the 2020 rule text; the July 2024 amendment was not read directly.

verification.topic: Reporting crimes: convictions and pleas (s. 455.227(1)(t); s. 475.25(1)(p))
verification.manual: Licensees must report a conviction, guilty plea or nolo contendere plea to a crime within 30 days, whether or not adjudication is withheld [s. 475.25(1)(p), F.S.; s. 455.227(1)(t), F.S.]
verification.finding: s. 455.227(1)(t), which applies to all DBPR licensees including real estate, makes it a ground for discipline to fail to report in writing to the board (here FREC), or to DBPR if there is no board, within 30 days after being convicted or found guilty of, or pleading nolo contendere or guilty to, a crime in any jurisdiction, regardless of adjudication. s. 475.25(1)(p) (2025) is narrower: discipline for failing to inform the Commission in writing within 30 days after pleading guilty or nolo contendere to, or being convicted or found guilty of, any FELONY. The manual's combined rule (any crime, regardless of adjudication) is correct through s. 455.227(1)(t); the chapter 475 provision alone covers only felonies.
verification.teach: Report in writing within 30 days any conviction or finding of guilt, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere, to ANY crime in any jurisdiction, regardless of adjudication (s. 455.227). Chapter 475 alone covers felonies.

verification.topic: Sales associate delivers deposits to the broker (Rule 61J2-14.009)
verification.manual: A sales associate must deliver a deposit to the employing broker no later than the end of the next business day [Rule 61J2-14.009, F.A.C.]
verification.finding: Every sales associate who receives any deposit (as defined in Rule 61J2-14.008) must deliver it to the broker or employer no later than the end of the next business day following receipt of the item to be deposited. Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays are not business days. Rulemaking authority is s. 475.05, F.S., and it implements s. 475.25(1)(k), F.S. The broker's own escrow deadline in 61J2-14.008 ('immediately', 3 business days) is a separate, longer rule.
verification.citation: Rule 61J2-14.009, F.A.C. (current text on flrules.org; last substantive amendment 2-5-04 per search excerpt); s. 475.25(1)(k), F.S. (2025)
verification.teach: By the end of the next business day after receipt (weekends and legal holidays are not business days).

verification.manual: 'Immediately' means the broker places escrow funds in an escrow account no later than the end of the third business day following receipt [Rule 61J2-14.008, F.A.C.]
verification.finding: Rule 61J2-14.008 defines 'immediately' as placing a deposit in an escrow account no later than the end of the third business day following receipt of the item to be deposited. Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays are not business days. The DBPR Bureau of Enforcement FAQ gives the same definition. The rule's history reads 'Amended 7-5-95, 7-4-06, 12-6-07, 6-21-10', and the excerpts show no later amendment.
verification.citation: Rule 61J2-14.008, F.A.C. (Definitions; effective 6-21-2010, current); implements s. 475.25(1)(k), F.S. (2025)
verification.teach: By the end of the third business day after receipt; weekends and legal holidays excluded. Received Monday → deposited by the end of Thursday.

verification.topic: Broker's own money in escrow accounts (Rule 61J2-14.010; s. 475.25(1)(k))
verification.manual: A broker may keep up to $1,000 of personal or brokerage funds in a sales escrow account and up to $5,000 in a property management escrow account [Rule 61J2-14.010, F.A.C.]
verification.finding: Rule 61J2-14.010(2): a broker may place and maintain up to $1,000 of personal or brokerage funds per sales escrow account and up to $5,000 per property management escrow account. The 2025 text of s. 475.25(1)(k), F.S. says the same: up to $5,000 in the property management escrow account and up to $1,000 in the sales escrow account. The statute adds that a broker gets a reasonable time to correct escrow errors when there is no shortage of funds and no significant threat of economic harm to the public, and that the Legislature intends disbursement of escrowed funds not to be delayed by a dispute over the personal or brokerage funds. One scraped copy of the rule also contained a general '$5,000 per account' sentence. The account-specific $1,000 sales cap governs and matches the statute.
verification.teach: Up to $1,000 in a sales escrow account; up to $5,000 in a property management escrow account.

verification.topic: Deposits held by a title company or attorney (Rule 61J2-14.008(2)(b))
verification.manual: When a deposit is held by a title company or attorney, the broker is not the escrow holder; the broker must obtain written verification of the deposit (manual: request a written statement and give it to the seller within 10 business days) [Rule 61J2-14.008, F.A.C.; s. 475.25(1)(d), F.S.]
verification.finding: The current rule has two separate 10-business-day steps plus an exception. (1) The licensee who prepared or presented the sales contract must put the title company's or attorney's name, address and telephone number on the contract. (2) Within 10 business days after each deposit is due under the sales contract, the licensee's broker must make a written request to the title company or attorney for written verification that the deposit was received. This step is not required if the seller or seller's agent nominated the title company or attorney in writing. (3) Within 10 business days of the date of that request, the broker must give the seller's broker (or the seller, if unrepresented) either a copy of the verification or written notice that no verification was received. What changed: before the 6-21-2010 amendment, the request was due within 3 business days after the deposit was due. The 2009 F.A.W. notice and an older rule file show the 3-day text; the current Chapter 61J2-14 compilation and FREC citation documents show 10 days. The manual's single 'give it to the seller within 10 business days' merges the two windows, leaves out the seller-nominated exception and the contract-disclosure duty, and names the seller instead of the seller's broker. The verification duty comes from the rule, not s. 475.25(1)(d); s. 475.25(1)(k) is what allows deposits to be held by a title company.
verification.teach: The contract names the title company or attorney (name, address, phone). Within 10 business days after each deposit is due, the broker asks the holder in writing to verify receipt (not required if the seller or seller's agent nominated the holder in writing). Within 10 business days of that request, the broker gives the seller's broker (or the seller, if unrepresented) the verification or a notice that none was received.

verification.manual: Brokers must keep books, accounts and records (including escrow records and disclosures) for at least 5 years; if litigation is involved, at least 2 years after it concludes [Rule 61J2-14.012, F.A.C.; s. 475.5015, F.S.]
verification.finding: s. 475.5015, F.S.: each broker must keep at least one legible copy of all books, accounts and records of the brokerage business for at least 5 years. The 5 years run from receipt of any entrusted money, fund, deposit, check or draft or, if no funds were entrusted, from the date any party signs the listing agreement, offer to purchase, rental property management agreement, lease or other agreement engaging the broker. If a document is the subject of litigation or used as evidence in it, the relevant records must be kept at least 2 years after the civil action or any appellate proceeding concludes, whichever is later, and never less than 5 years in total. Rule 61J2-14.012 separately requires the broker to preserve deposit slips, depository statements and the parties' agreements and make them available to the Department. It also requires an accurate account of each deposit and each bank account, plus monthly reconciliations. The retention periods themselves come from the statute, not the rule excerpt.
verification.teach: Keep at least 5 years (from receipt of funds or, if none, from signing of the listing, offer, lease or other agreement). In litigation: at least 2 years after the case and any appeal end, and never less than 5 years in total.

verification.manual: FREC may impose an administrative fine of up to $5,000 per count and suspend a license for up to 10 years [s. 475.25(1), F.S.]
verification.finding: s. 475.25(1), F.S.: the Commission may deny an application or renewal, place a licensee on probation, suspend a license, registration or permit for up to 10 years, revoke it, impose an administrative fine of up to $5,000 for each count or separate offense, and issue a reprimand, on the listed grounds. Wording is identical in the 2024 and 2025 editions. The cap was $1,000 per count in the 2002 edition and was $5,000 by the 2010 edition. The 2026 edition is listed on the official site; the excerpts showed no change, but its subsection (1) penalty text was not retrieved.
verification.teach: Fine up to $5,000 per count; suspension up to 10 years; also denial, probation, revocation and reprimand.

verification.manual: The probable cause panel for real estate is composed of two members, at least one a current FREC member (other may be a former member) [s. 455.225(4), F.S.; s. 475.021?]
verification.finding: s. 455.225(4), F.S.: probable cause is decided by majority vote of a board's probable cause panel. A board may set up by rule multiple panels of at least two members, and one or more panel members may be former board members. Every panel must include a present board member and a former or present professional member, and a former professional member must hold an active valid license. It must also include a former or present consumer member if one is available, willing to serve and authorized by the chair. FREC Rule 61J2-20.009 (effective 11-8-2012): per FREC 2016/2019 rule documents, the panel must include at least one present Commission member, and one member may be a former Commission member, as s. 455.225(4) allows. A 2012 FREC meeting copy of the rule read 'two current members of the Commission,' appointed by the chair. The exact panel size in the current rule text was not seen directly, but a two-member panel fits both the statute and the rule. The authority is s. 455.225(4) and Rule 61J2-20.009, not s. 475.021.
verification.teach: At least two members, including a present FREC member; a former member may serve. Probable cause is decided by majority vote. (Current rule wording on size seen only in fragments.)

verification.manual: A licensee may appeal a final order to the District Court of Appeal within 30 days [s. 120.68, F.S.; Fla. R. App. P. 9.110]
verification.finding: s. 120.68, F.S.: a party adversely affected by final agency action may seek judicial review. All proceedings start by filing a notice of appeal or petition for review under the Florida Rules of Appellate Procedure within 30 days after rendition of the order appealed. Review is in the appellate district where the agency has its headquarters or where a party resides, or as otherwise provided by law. Fla. R. App. P. 9.110(c): for appeals of final orders of lower administrative tribunals, the notice is filed with the agency clerk within 30 days of rendition, and a copy with filing fees goes to the court clerk. Missing the 30-day notice is an irremediable jurisdictional defect.
verification.citation: s. 120.68(1)(a), (2)(a), F.S. (2025; 2026 edition excerpt identical); Fla. R. App. P. 9.110(c)
verification.teach: Notice of appeal within 30 days after the final order is rendered, to the District Court of Appeal.

verification.manual: All licensee advertising must include the licensed name of the brokerage firm (blind ad otherwise); rules for team names and internet ads (firm name placement) [Rule 61J2-10.025, F.A.C.]
verification.finding: Confirmed, but the team-name rules are in a different rule than the manual says. Rule 61J2-10.025(1) says all advertising must let reasonable people know they are dealing with a real estate licensee, and every real estate advertisement must include the licensed name of the brokerage firm. Ads may not be fraudulent, false, deceptive or misleading. (2): if the licensee's personal name appears, at least the last name must be used as registered with the Commission. (3)(a), internet ads: the brokerage firm name must be placed next to, or directly above or below, the 'point of contact information'. That term means any way to contact the brokerage or the licensee: mailing or street address, email, telephone or fax. The flrules chapter index still lists 2/5/2007 as the effective date. An amendment proposed in 2018-2019 (licensee name no larger than the brokerage name; individual licensees barred from words like 'Brokerage', 'Brokers', 'Company') was not confirmed as adopted, so treat it as unverified. TEAM NAMES are in Rule 61J2-10.026 (Team or Group Advertising, effective 11/1/2021), not 10.025: (a) the team must work under the same broker and file a designated licensee with the broker; (b) the broker keeps a written roster of team members, updated at least monthly; (c) team names may include 'team' or 'group' but not 'Brokerage', 'Realty', 'Real Estate', 'Properties', 'Company' or similar words suggesting a separate brokerage; (d) ads with the team name may not be in larger print than the registered brokerage's name or logo; (e) ads must make clear to reasonable people that they are dealing with a team or group. Failing to include the registered brokerage name can be cited under Rule 61J2-24.002.
verification.citation: Rule 61J2-10.025(1)-(3), F.A.C. (eff. 2/5/2007, current per flrules chapter index, 2026); Rule 61J2-10.026, F.A.C. (eff. 11/1/2021) for team or group advertising
verification.teach: Every ad includes the licensed brokerage name (otherwise it is a blind ad). A licensee's own name: at least the last name as registered. Internet ads: brokerage name next to, above or below the contact information. Team names may use 'team' or 'group' but not 'Brokerage', 'Realty', 'Real Estate', 'Properties', 'Company' or similar, and may not appear larger than the brokerage name.

verification.manual: Broker's office entrance sign must show the broker's name, trade name if any, and 'Licensed Real Estate Broker' or 'Lic. Real Estate Broker' [Rule 61J2-10.024, F.A.C.]
verification.finding: Confirmed. The operative requirement is in statute s. 475.22(1), F.S. (2025). Each active broker must keep a sign on or about the entrance of the principal office and each branch office, where anyone about to enter can easily see and read it. The sign must contain the broker's name together with the trade name, if any. For a partnership or corporation, it must show the firm's name or trade name and the name of at least one active broker. At a minimum, the words 'licensed real estate broker' or 'lic. real estate broker' must appear on office entrance signs. Rule 61J2-10.024 (Office Entrance Signs) still appears on flrules. A repeal was proposed in January 2006 on the ground that it only duplicates Chapter 475, but flrules marks it 'Not Adopted by FAC Yet'. Whether or not the rule stands, the statute imposes the same requirement. Older versions (2002/2010) said the Commission set the sign's form and minimum dimensions; the 2025 excerpt does not show that language.
verification.citation: s. 475.22(1), F.S. (2025; the 2026 edition carries the same section heading); Rule 61J2-10.024, F.A.C. (2006 proposed repeal not adopted)
verification.teach: At the entrance of the main office and each branch: the broker's name and any trade name (a firm: its name plus at least one broker) and the words 'Licensed Real Estate Broker' or 'Lic. Real Estate Broker'.

verification.manual: Designated sales associates allowed only in nonresidential transactions where buyer and seller each have assets of $1 million or more and request it in writing [s. 475.2755, F.S.]
verification.finding: Confirmed. In a real estate transaction other than a 'residential sale' as defined in s. 475.278(5)(a), a broker may, at the customers' request, designate sales associates to act as single agents for different customers in the same transaction. This is allowed only where the buyer and seller have assets of $1 million or more. A 'residential sale' is improved residential property of four units or fewer, unimproved residential property intended for four units or fewer, or agricultural property of 10 acres or fewer. The buyer and seller must both sign disclosures stating that their assets meet the threshold and asking the broker to use the designated sales associate form of representation. Designated sales associates have a single agent's duties under s. 475.278(3), including the (3)(b)-(c) disclosure requirements. They may not disclose confidential customer information except to the broker or persons the broker specifies (or as the law permits or requires). The broker must keep that information confidential and may not use it to the detriment of the other party. The $1 million figure is unchanged from the 2000/2002 editions through the 2024 and 2026 editions.
verification.citation: s. 475.2755, F.S. (2026 ed.; same text in 2024); s. 475.278(5)(a), F.S. for 'residential sale'
verification.teach: Only in nonresidential transactions; buyer and seller each have assets of $1 million or more and sign disclosures requesting it. Each designated associate has a single agent's duties.

verification.manual: The fact that a property was the site of a homicide, suicide or death, or that an occupant had HIV/AIDS, is not a material fact that must be disclosed [s. 689.25, F.S.]
verification.finding: Confirmed. s. 689.25(1)(a): the fact that an occupant of real property is or has been infected with HIV, or diagnosed with AIDS, is not a material fact that must be disclosed in a real estate transaction. (1)(b): the fact that a property was, or was at any time suspected to have been, the site of a homicide, suicide or death is not a material fact that must be disclosed in a real estate transaction. (2): no cause of action arises against an owner, the owner's agent, a transferee's agent, or a person licensed under chapter 475 for failing to disclose these facts. The 2001 version covered only HIV/AIDS; the homicide, suicide and death language was added later and is in the 2010 through 2025 text. The 2026 index still lists s. 689.25 under the same title ('Failure to disclose homicide, suicide, deaths, or diagnosis of HIV or AIDS infection in an occupant of real property').
verification.citation: s. 689.25(1)(a)-(b), (2), F.S. (2025; listed unchanged in the 2026 index)
verification.teach: That a homicide, suicide or death occurred on the property, or that an occupant had HIV/AIDS, is not a material fact that must be disclosed.

verification.manual: Single agent notice: before or at the time of entering a listing/representation agreement or before showing property, whichever occurs first; No brokerage relationship notice: before showing; consent to transition before the change [s. 475.278(3)-(4), F.S.]
verification.finding: Confirmed. s. 475.278(3)(b): a single agent's duties must be fully described and disclosed in writing to the buyer or seller. This can be a separate document or part of another document such as a listing or representation agreement. The disclosure must be made before, or at the time of, entering into a listing agreement or an agreement for representation, or before the showing of property, whichever occurs first. If included in another document, the notice must be at least as large as the other provisions and conspicuously placed, with the first sentence in uppercase bold type, using the prescribed 'SINGLE AGENT NOTICE' form. s. 475.278(3)(c): a single agent may transition to transaction broker only if the principal gives written consent before the change in relationship, using the prescribed Consent to Transition to Transaction Broker notice. s. 475.278(4): a licensee with no brokerage relationship must disclose its duties in writing before the showing of property, using the prescribed notice. These disclosure requirements apply only to residential sales (s. 475.274, s. 475.278(5)). They do not apply to nonresidential transactions, most rentals or leases, bona fide open houses or model home showings that involve no eliciting of confidential information or negotiation, or when the licensee knows the party is already represented by a single agent or transaction broker.
verification.teach: Single agent notice: before or at the time of a listing or representation agreement, or before showing property, whichever comes first. No brokerage relationship notice: before showing property. Single agent → transaction broker: the principal's written consent before the change.

verification.manual: Written listing agreements must have a definite expiration date, description, price and terms, fee, signatures; no automatic renewal; copy delivered to the person signing within 24 hours [s. 475.25(1)(r), F.S.]
verification.finding: Confirmed, with one note on wording. Under s. 475.25(1)(r), the Commission may discipline a licensee who fails to include required terms in a written listing agreement or to deliver a copy on time. Each written listing agreement must contain a definite expiration date, a description of the property, price and terms, the fee or commission, and the signature of the principal(s). A copy must be given to the person signing within 24 hours of obtaining the written listing agreement. The statute does not use the words 'automatic renewal'. Instead it says a written listing agreement may contain no provision requiring the person signing to notify the broker of an intention to cancel after the definite expiration date. In effect, that bars self-renewing listings that need a cancellation notice. The provision applies to written listing agreements; it does not require every listing to be in writing.
verification.teach: Definite expiration date, property description, price and terms, fee, principal's signature; copy to the signer within 24 hours; no clause requiring the seller to give notice to cancel after the expiration date (no automatic renewal).

verification.manual: Loan Estimate delivered within 3 business days after receiving the application [12 CFR 1026.19(e)] / Closing Disclosure received at least 3 business days before consummation [12 CFR 1026.19(f)]
verification.finding: The creditor must deliver or mail the Loan Estimate no later than the third business day after it receives the consumer's application, as defined in 1026.2(a)(3). The clock starts once the six application items in 1026.2(a)(3)(ii) are received. For this deadline, 'business day' has the general meaning: a day the creditor's offices are open to the public for carrying on substantially all of its business functions. Separately, 1026.19(e)(1)(iii)(B) requires the Loan Estimate to be delivered or mailed no later than the seventh business day before consummation, and for that rule a business day is every calendar day except Sundays and federal legal public holidays. Mailed or emailed Loan Estimates are treated as received 3 business days after delivery or mailing. If the creditor denies the application, or the consumer withdraws it, within the 3-day window, no Loan Estimate is required. No 2025 or 2026 final rule changing this timing was found; a July 9, 2026 CFPB request for information only asks for comment. Under 1026.19(f)(1)(ii)(A), the creditor must ensure the consumer receives the Closing Disclosure no later than three business days before consummation. Exceptions are listed in (f)(1)(ii)(B) (timeshares: by consummation) and in (f)(2). Disclosures not handed over in person are treated as received 3 business days after delivery or mailing. For this rule, a business day is every calendar day except Sundays and federal legal public holidays, so Saturdays count. A consumer may waive the waiting period only for a bona fide personal financial emergency, and only after receiving the disclosures. Under (f)(2)(ii), a corrected Closing Disclosure starts a new 3-business-day waiting period if the APR becomes inaccurate, the loan product changes, or a prepayment penalty is added. No 2025 or 2026 timing amendment was found.
verification.citation: 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(1)(iii)(A)-(B) and 1026.2(a)(6), Regulation Z (eCFR current text, 2026; official comment 19(e)(1)(iii)); 12 CFR 1026.19(f)(1)(ii)(A), (f)(1)(iii)-(iv), (f)(2)(ii), Regulation Z (eCFR current text, 2026)
verification.teach: Loan Estimate: delivered or mailed within 3 business days after the application. Closing Disclosure: received at least 3 business days before consummation; a new 3-day wait only if the APR becomes inaccurate, the loan product changes or a prepayment penalty is added.

verification.manual: TILA right of rescission: 3 business days for credit secured by the consumer's principal dwelling; not for residential mortgage transactions (purchase money) [12 CFR 1026.23]
verification.finding: Under 1026.23(a)(1), in a credit transaction where a security interest is or will be retained or acquired in a consumer's principal dwelling, each consumer whose ownership interest is or will be subject to it has the right to rescind. The right runs until midnight of the third business day after the latest of three events: consummation, delivery of the rescission notice, or delivery of all material disclosures. If the notice or material disclosures are never delivered, the right expires 3 years after consummation, or earlier on transfer of all the consumer's interest or on sale of the property. For rescission, business days include Saturdays but not Sundays or federal legal public holidays. Under 1026.23(f), the right does not apply to (1) a residential mortgage transaction, meaning credit to finance the purchase or initial construction of the principal dwelling, or (2) a refinancing by the same creditor, except to the extent the new amount financed exceeds the unpaid principal, earned unpaid finance charges and refinancing costs. If the consumer rescinds, the security interest becomes void and the consumer owes no finance charge.
verification.citation: 12 CFR 1026.23(a)(1), (a)(3), (d)(1), (f) and 1026.2(a)(6), Regulation Z (eCFR current text; CFR 2025 edition, govinfo)
verification.teach: 3 business days (Saturdays count) for credit secured by the borrower's principal dwelling, such as a home equity loan or a refinance with a new lender. Not for loans to buy or build the home.

verification.manual: Advertising trigger terms: amount or percentage of down payment, number of payments or period of repayment, amount of any payment, amount of any finance charge [12 CFR 1026.24(d)]
verification.finding: For closed-end credit, 1026.24(d)(1) lists four triggering terms: (i) the amount or percentage of any downpayment; (ii) the number of payments or period of repayment; (iii) the amount of any payment; (iv) the amount of any finance charge. An ad that states any one of them must also state the items in (d)(2): the downpayment amount or percentage, the terms of repayment (including any balloon payment), and the APR, with a note if the rate may increase after consummation. The official commentary adds four points. Implied terms count; for example, '80 percent financing' implies a 20% downpayment. 'No downpayment' is not a trigger. Vague phrases such as 'monthly payments to suit your needs' are not statements of a payment amount. Stating the APR, or that there is no particular charge (for example 'no closing costs'), is not a trigger.
